docs.title: batchdx-cyto
docs.text:
Batch-effect diagnosis, correction and evaluation for mass cytometry, conventional flow cytometry and spectral flow cytometry, orchestrated by Snakemake.

Scope: synthetic fixtures only. This package ships no real cytometry dataset or real-data example. Its scientific checks use simulated data; its thresholds are not calibrated for a real cohort. See validation limits.

Built for cross-cohort immune studies, where biological differences and technical batches are often correlated and where the honest answer is frequently "this contrast cannot be corrected".

Status: 0.1.0 — research preview. The Python core, the design audit, the diagnostics, the metrics (including seven verified against pinned upstream components), the decision layer, the report and the Snakemake workflow run end to end and are tested, including real Snakemake executions and the R-backed cyCombine and CytoNorm paths against their pinned upstream checkouts. Three things you must know before using it:

  1. Every decision threshold is an uncalibrated engineering default. The report says so next to every recommendation. Do not cite the thresholds as validated cutoffs.
  2. No real-data validation yet. All evidence comes from synthetic fixtures of 250–2,000 cells per sample. Production CyTOF acquisitions are orders of magnitude larger; expect the memory and runtime profile to be untested.
  3. CytoNorm and PeacoQC execute for real at their pinned versions, and CI builds the full R environment (cyCombine, CytoNorm, PeacoQC, flowVS) from the pinned local checkouts, so the R-backed tests run there too. They remain the least exercised backends, and their GPL licences mean they are called, never vendored.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Diagnoses batch-associated differences and asks whether a technical interpretation is actually supported by the design.
  2. Runs eligible correction methods independently, always including an identity candidate, because "no correction" is a valid result.
  3. Evaluates technical improvement and, separately, what the correction did to the data's structure — including whether the biological contrast of interest survived.
  4. Reports: one offline HTML file, structured JSON/CSV records, and corrected datasets with an explicit scale.

Three things it deliberately refuses to do:

  • It will not turn association into attribution. A batch contrast is classified as reference_supported, biologically_stratified_conditional, descriptive_only or non_identifiable, and perfect confounding blocks automatic recommendations for the affected contrast. Adding the confounded factor as a covariate does not fix it, and the audit says so.
  • It will not invent evidence. An unavailable dependency, an invalid comparison, an absent control or a failed method gets an explicit status and a reason. A missing metric is never a zero, and a near-zero denominator is undefined, not an epsilon.
  • It will not recommend under uncalibrated thresholds. A candidate that clears every gate under the shipped policies reaches eligible_for_review, never recommended_under_policy. Automatic approval requires a policy whose thresholds carry a declared calibration — which means doing the calibration.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install -e '.[workflow]'
batchdx-cyto init my-project --example paired_reference
batchdx-cyto benchmark --config my-project/config/config.yaml \
    --outdir my-project/results/run1 --cores 4

Then open my-project/results/run1/report/report.html — one offline file, no server. The quickstart vignette walks through a full run and reads the decision with you.

docs.title: Compatibility matrix
docs.text:
What is actually known about the versions and backends this package runs on, and — for every row — the command that establishes it.

The rule this file follows. A cell says verified only if a command was run on this checkout and produced the stated result. It says declared-only when a tracked file asserts it but nothing here executed it. It says untested when there is neither. No row is verified because a version number looks plausible. Where a number was resolved from a remote index over the network, that is stated in the row, because "resolved" and "ran" are different claims.

Measured on 2026-09-30 at commit 9850c33 plus uncommitted work in the tree.

Environment of record. Python 3.12.13, R 4.4.3 (renv/bin/R), .venv for Python and renv/lib/R/library for R. Every verified cell below was measured here.

docs.title: Tested versus declared, reconciled
docs.text:
Four tracked files made four different statements about which Python this package runs on, and the disagreement was itself the defect:

Source Said pyproject.toml requires-python >=3.10 — a floor, i.e. everything at or above 3.10 is permitted pyproject.toml classifiers 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 — four versions advertised .github/workflows/batchdx-cyto-tests.yaml:29 python-version: "3.12" — configured for CI, with no completed runner job yet workflow/envs/python.yaml:29 python=3.12 — one version pinned for the workflow

A floor, a classifier list, a CI pin and an environment pin are four different claims, and only two of them are ever executed. The reconciliation is deliberately boring: 3.12 is the tested version; the other three are declared. Nothing is widened to make the table look better, and no version is marked verified because a number next to it looks plausible.

Version Status What was actually run How to verify 3.12 verified the suite in two runs: .venv/bin/python -V → Python 3.12.13; pytest -q tests/unit → 123 passed in 25s; pytest -q tests/scientific → 95 passed / 1 skipped in 1m47s; together 243 passed / 1 skipped in 2m13s, of which 25 are tests/scientific/test_multiseed.py python -V; .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit tests/scientific 3.11 declared-only nothing. No environment was built and no test was run. A grammar-level parse of all 85 .py files under 3.11 succeeds, which rules out a syntax regression and establishes nothing else python3.11 -m venv .venv311 && .venv311/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]' && .venv311/bin/pytest -q 3.10 declared-only nothing. Same as 3.11: grammar-level parse only. This is the requires-python floor, so a 3.10 incompatibility is a packaging bug, not an untested feature as above, with python3.10 3.13 declared-only nothing. Grammar-level parse only. A trove classifier with no environment behind it is a claim; it is labelled as one as above, with python3.13

The grammar-level check, and exactly what it is. All 85 .py files under src/, tests/ and scripts/ were parsed with ast.parse(..., feature_version=(3, N)) for N in 10, 11, 12, 13; all 85 parse under all four. That establishes that the source uses no syntax newer than 3.10, which is a real constraint on the requires-python floor and is the only thing about 3.10 that can be checked without installing a stack. It establishes nothing about the standard library surface, C-extension ABI, or dependency resolution, all of which differ across these versions.

python - <<'PY'
import ast, pathlib
files = list(pathlib.Path("src").rglob("*.py")) + list(pathlib.Path("tests").rglob("*.py"))
for minor in (10, 11, 12, 13):
    for p in files:
        ast.parse(p.read_text(), filename=str(p), feature_version=(3, minor))
print("all", len(files), "files parse under 3.10-3.13")
PY

There is no CI matrix across versions. The workflow names Python 3.12, matching the workflow environment. Three of the four rows above remain claims, not measurements, until a matrix runs. The Python 3.12 draft-PR job reached the complete suite on a GitHub runner in run 37102250467: 375 passed, 2 skipped and 2 interrupted-run byte comparisons failed. This is executed 3.12 evidence, not yet a green compatibility result.

docs.title: Dependency bounds: lower bounds only, and what that costs
docs.text:
All twelve core dependencies and all three metrics-extra dependencies carry a lower bound and no upper bound. That is a real gap, not a stylistic one, and the anndata>=0.10 line has already produced a user-visible failure:

  • What happened. anndata 0.13 added a None key to .layers that aliases .X. Any code that iterates or sorts the layer view hits it. io/dataset.py:361-364 filters if name is not None and is correct; io/dataset.py:255 does not, and still does sorted(adata.layers) in an error message. With anndata 0.13.4 a file carrying both a None key and a named layer raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType' where the intended DatasetValidationError should name the available layers. Reproduce it with: 
    import anndata as ad, numpy as np
a = ad.AnnData(X=np.zeros((3, 2), dtype="float32")); a.layers["preprocessed"] = np.zeros((3, 2))
sorted(a.layers)   # TypeError
sorted(n for n in a.layers if n is not None)   # the fix already applied at :361-364
    A TypeError from a library's error path is the worst of both: the message is unreadable and the validation it was written to perform never runs.
  • Why one fix does not close the class. A lower bound cannot express "and not the version that changed this". Only an upper bound, or a version matrix, stops the next one. pandas 3.0 and numpy 2.x are the same shape of risk and have not yet broken anything here, which is luck rather than a bound.

Recommended bounds. These are recommendations, not edits — pyproject.toml is not this tranche's to change. Each ceiling is the next major version above the one row in the table above that was actually executed, so the bound is "everything up to and including what we ran", which is the most that can honestly be promised.

Package Now Recommended Ceiling rationale numpy >=1.24 >=1.24,<3 2.x changed the ABI and scalar promotion; 3 is untested pandas >=2.0 >=2.0,<4 3.0 is a major release (copy-on-write, removals); 4 is untested scipy >=1.10 >=1.10,<2 1.x is tested; 2 is untested anndata >=0.10 >=0.10,<0.14 the live one: 0.13 changed .layers semantics h5py >=3.8 >=3.8,<4 3.x is tested; 4 is untested pydantic >=2.5 >=2.5,<3 2.x is tested; 3 is untested typer >=0.9 >=0.9,<1 pre-1.0: the ceiling is 1.0, not 0.28 jinja2 >=3.1 >=3.1,<4 3.x is tested; 4 is untested pyyaml >=6.0 >=6.0,<7 6.x is tested; 7 is untested flowio >=1.2 >=1.2,<2 1.x is tested; 2 is untested pyarrow >=14.0 >=14.0,<26 25.0.1 is tested; 26 is untested matplotlib >=3.7 >=3.7,<4 3.x is tested; 4 is untested snakemake (workflow) >=8.0 >=8.0,<10 9.27.0 is tested; the 8→9 jump moved APIs scikit-learn (metrics) >=1.3 >=1.3,<2 1.9.1 is tested; 2 is untested scib-metrics (metrics) >=0.5 >=0.5,<0.7 0.6.1 is tested; pre-1.0 ceiling is the minor umap-learn (metrics) >=0.5 >=0.5,<0.6 0.5.12 is tested; pre-1.0 ceiling is the minor

The lower bounds are the larger half of the problem and ceilings do not touch them. numpy>=1.24 permits 1.24, which has never been run here; pandas>=2.0 permits 2.0; and so on down the table. A ceiling stops the next breaking release; only a lowest-supported-dependency job — a second CI job that resolves every dependency to its floor and runs the suite — turns those promises into measurements. Neither exists today, and no row in this file claims otherwise.

docs.title: R-side test coverage
docs.text:
R is not an optional garnish here: eight R files under scripts/ and workflow/scripts/ do work that batchdx.cyto.pipeline drives, which is why Programming Language :: R is declared in pyproject.toml. Until this tranche, one of them (scripts/audit_upstream.R) was the only one CI executed.

R file Unit tests Driven end to end by pytest workflow/scripts/lib/binmat.R yes — tests/testthat/test-binmat.R, 101 assertions yes, tests/unit/test_contracts.py:124-165 workflow/scripts/cycombine_correct.R no yes — cyCombine correction runs at its pinned commit workflow/scripts/cycombine_detect.R no yes — Stage 5 native-detector comparison workflow/scripts/cytobatchflagr_detect.R no no — never executed, see B-006 below workflow/scripts/cycombine_evaluate.R no no workflow/scripts/cytonorm_correct.R no yes — CytoNorm backend, 4/4 workflow/scripts/peacoqc_qc.R no yes — tests/integration/test_peacoqc_backend.py scripts/audit_upstream.R no yes — CI, and the Stage 0 gate

binmat.R is the one covered directly, and it is covered directly on purpose: its own header calls it a hand-mirror of io/binary.py, and it is the only file in the package where a byte-order or row-major/column-major divergence would be silent and would corrupt every adapter. tests/testthat/test-binmat.R holds both implementations to a contract stated by neither of them — the expected bytes are produced by base R writeBin against a raw() connection — so a divergence cannot hide behind a matching divergence. The suite currently reports 94 passing and 7 failing, all 7 from one defect in binmat.R:49 (auto_unbox = TRUE collapses a length-1 row_ids/col_names to a JSON scalar, which Python's list(...) then iterates character by character). See the tranche report for the one-line fix and the verified blast radius.

Run the R suite with:

Rscript --vanilla tests/run_r_tests.R          # exits non-zero on any failure
BATCHDX_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python Rscript --vanilla tests/run_r_tests.R   # force cross-language

docs.title: CytoBatchFlagR execution and limits
docs.text:
The enforced dependency set is the 29 unconditional library() calls at .upstream/CytoBatchFlagR/R/CytoBatchFlagR_functions.R:6-34. All 29 load in the isolated R environment. The integration test calls the pinned source, observes the injected flag, and checks the unshifted design. The earlier tests that stopped at an eligibility guard remain useful refusal-path tests; the new integration tests reach R.

The 1.5-IQR fence has a high per-test false-positive rate at realistic batch counts, so flag=True is an uncalibrated finding. The adapter also requires at least 100 cells per control and marker to avoid treating a dropped control as a clean result. See docs/blocked.md B-006 for the measured specificity limitation and rationale.

Check the executed path with:

.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/integration/test_cytobatchflagr_backend.py

docs.title: OpenProblems compatibility components
docs.text:
Seven of the nine OpenProblems metric names are registered in this package's compatibility namespace with upstream_verified=True. "Verified" here has one specific meaning: a test imports the pinned Viash helper from the pinned checkout and compares its output against ours under the tolerance below. Six were executed on 2026-09-30 and passed; the FlowSOM component was executed on 2026-10-16 and passed.

Component Pinned helper Tolerance asserted by the test Status Test emd_mean_ct_horiz emd/helper.py rel=1e-9 verified test_the_pinned_horizontal_emd_matches_the_extracted_component emd_mean_ct_vert emd/helper.py rel=1e-9 verified test_the_pinned_vertical_emd_matches_the_extracted_component ratio_consistent_peaks ratio_consistent_peaks/helper.py rtol=0, atol=1e-12 on density; exact array equality on the counts verified test_the_pinned_peak_helpers_reproduce_the_extracted_ones average_batch_r2_ct average_batch_r2/helper.py rel=1e-9, abs=1e-12 per marker and on the aggregate verified test_the_pinned_batch_r2_helper_matches_the_extracted_component iLisi lisi/helper.py rtol=0, atol=0 per cell; rel=1e-12, abs=1e-15 on the normalisation verified test_the_pinned_lisi_helpers_match_the_extracted_ones cLisi lisi/helper.py rtol=0, atol=0 per cell; rel=1e-12, abs=1e-15 on the normalisation verified test_the_pinned_lisi_helpers_match_the_extracted_ones flowsom_mean_mapping_similarity flowsom_mapping_similarity/helper.R abs=1e-8 on the similarity, the percentage tables and the weights, the pinned R functions run on shared assignment vectors verified test_the_pinned_flowsom_helper_matches_the_local_pipeline

All seven node IDs above are in tests/scientific/test_stage7_openproblems.py. Three supporting helpers are verified the same way and are worth knowing about because they are what the deferred rows would build on: test_the_pinned_bin_array_reproduces_the_extracted_one, test_the_pinned_compute_emd_reproduces_the_extracted_distance, test_the_pinned_wilcoxon_helper_matches_the_local_rank_statistic and test_the_pinned_cohens_d_helper_matches_the_local_cohens_d.

The FlowSOM component is a named adaptation, not a copy of the pinned assembly. The pinned script.R reads its three parameters from the unintegrated file's .uns (parameter_num_clusters, parameter_som_xdim, parameter_som_ydim) and builds one tree per donor per split, mapping each split through the other; this package has no such file and one candidate per frozen partition, so the three parameters are declared constants on the metric spec (num_clusters=15, som_xdim=10, som_ydim=10, with the pinned seed=42), one tree is built on the reference batch -- the batch holding the most evaluation cells, ties broken lexicographically -- and every other batch is mapped into it with FlowSOM::NewData. What is not adapted is the arithmetic: the pinned compute_clust_pct, compute_clust_weights and the weighted-difference formula are executed in R on the same assignment vectors the local implementation receives, and the two must agree to 1e-8.

docs.title: Data: this package ships no real cytometry data, and that is the design
docs.text:
Stated on the face of the documentation, not only in docs/blocked.md. This package ships no real cytometry data and no real-data example, because none is obtainable under the current egress policy. That is a scope decision, taken deliberately, not a gap waiting to be filled: no gate depends on real data, and no claim in this package is about real data.

The consequence is a hard limit on everything above. Every verified row in this file was measured against deterministic synthetic fixtures from batchdx.cyto.simulate. A version being exercised here means this code ran on this input; it does not mean the code has been exercised on anything a flow cytometrist would recognise. The specific things real data would test and these fixtures do not are heavy tails, multimodality, marker dropout, instrument artefacts and genuine spillover compensation.

Real data included none Real-data example included none Origin of every fixture batchdx.cyto.simulate — five populations, declared marker means, a shared within-population latent factor, and separately controllable batch_shift / batch_spread / group_shift / drift / frequency knobs Obstruction egress policy; no permissibly usable dataset with reference or replicate structure was obtainable, and none was written from memory Where it is stated docs/blocked.md B-008, docs/validation_results.md §4, examples/README.md, the README.md scope note, and here What would change it one permissibly licensed dataset with provenance and checksums, plus a run over it. Not a code change

Anyone reading a verified cell above should read this section with it. The compatibility of a library version is a real, transferable fact; the compatibility of this package's scientific conclusions is a statement about synthetic fixtures only.

docs.title: Not verified here, and why
docs.text:
Naming these is part of the matrix. Each one is a claim someone could otherwise make by omission.

  • The container. containers/Dockerfile.r-backends has never been built, run or pulled. Its base image digest was resolved over the Docker Hub registry HTTP API on 2026-09-30 — twice, same answer — and that is the only thing established about it. It is the digest of the multi-platform OCI index, not of any single platform image. Which repository each R package belongs to was checked against the live CRAN index and Bioconductor 3.20; whether the installs succeed was not.
  • CI. Draft PR #2 has executed both Python and R suites. The first complete Python report has two resilience failures; R exchange tests, Ruff, Snakemake lint and both upstream audits passed. A corrected complete run is pending.
  • Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13. Declared; the source parses under their grammars and nothing else about them was run.
  • Any R version other than 4.4.3.
  • Real cytometry data. See the section above: this is a stated scope boundary, and every scientific result in this package rests on synthetic fixtures.
  • The R-side test suite against every R script. tests/testthat/test-binmat.R covers workflow/scripts/lib/binmat.R, the exchange library every adapter loads. The adapter scripts are covered by Python integration tests that drive them end to end; the R exchange suite is now configured in CI, but has not run on a GitHub runner.

docs.title: Stage 2 (Tier A) — Ingestion, immutable data, preprocessing machinery (not yet in a run)
docs.text:
🟡 PARTIAL — 64 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 not executed.

Partial: 2-D gating, the per-panel asinh transform, the PeacoQC pass and a removed_events writer are implemented in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/ and tested against the pinned reference implementation's OWN configuration files, which load unchanged; the transform is verified element-wise against flowVS::transFlowVS, and logicle was removed from the schema because nothing here implements it. NOT satisfied: none of it is wired into a run. preprocess operates on raw events before a baseline exists, so there is no preprocessing stage, no Snakemake rule and no report section for the removal log, and every shipped example takes the already-QCed bypass path. A run must therefore still be handed preprocessed data, which is the behaviour this package documents. See docs/blocked.md B-009.

docs.title: Stage 4 (Tier B) — Freeze evaluation populations, sampling and splits
docs.text:
🟡 PARTIAL — 26 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 not executed.

Partial: Splits are implemented and enforced: sampling/splits.py partitions samples into train/tune/validate BY BIOSPECIMEN (donor, else biospecimen_id, else sample_id), the unit is recorded in the manifest rather than inferred by the reader, and decisions/policy.py refuses to let a contrast that only the training split can estimate support a recommendation (test_a_contrast_only_the_training_split_can_estimate_blocks_approval). NOT satisfied: the 60/20/20 proportions are uncalibrated engineering defaults with a declared origin, and they are not configurable by a user. On a design too thin to stratify the manifest is emitted with the deficiency reported as a coverage warning rather than refused, because refusing would take the detectors, metrics and report down with it; the fit-and-apply backend still refuses such a design itself.

docs.title: Report totals
docs.text:
The referenced report's raw counts are environment-dependent (a test that skips in one environment runs in another), so they are not reproduced here; the gate table above is the environment-independent statement.

Tests outside the gate lists (helpers and additional checks) are counted in the totals but do not decide a gate.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
pip install -e '.[dev]'     # from a checkout
batchdx-cyto info           # prints the backends, detectors and metrics this build ships

batchdx-cyto info --json is the authoritative answer to "can this build do X". It reports, per backend, whether fit-and-apply is supported and whether that support has been verified, which parameters are accepted, and which are refused and why.

The R backends need an R environment on top. See containers/Dockerfile.r-backends — not built or tested in this build — and docs/blocked.md.

docs.title: 2. Preparing input
docs.text: The package reads preprocessed data and refuses to guess what has been done to it.

docs.title: The expression object
docs.text: Either an H5AD with the values in a named layer (declared as input.expression_layer; X is never used implicitly), or a directory of FCS files with one file per sample named in the sample manifest.

docs.title: samples.tsv
docs.text:
One row per measured sample. Only sample_id is required; everything else enables something specific.

Column Enables sample_id required batch every batch contrast donor_id donor-matched metrics, n_donors on every metric record, and the donor-paired model (with bootstrap uncertainty intervals) behind every biological-preservation record biospecimen_id, aliquot_id recorded on SampleRecord and kept distinct in every emitted manifest, so the levels cannot be silently merged. Nothing in this build reads them group, stimulation, timepoint protected factors and stratified contrasts reference_id + reference_role reference-supported evidence, CytoNorm, CytoBatchFlagR

Any other column is kept as a technical factor and can be named as design.correction_batch or design.nested_within.

reference_role is one of none, technical_replicate, anchor, biological_pseudo_control. Declaring a role without a reference_id is an error, because reference identity is never inferred from file names. Only technical_replicate and anchor count as measured technical evidence; biological_pseudo_control never does, whatever the configuration says.

The same donor at two timepoints, or under two stimulations, is not a technical replicate. The package will not treat it as one.

docs.title: markers.tsv
docs.text:
Column Meaning feature_id required, unique channel required for FCS input; must map one-to-one to feature_id marker, panel_id labels; more than one panel_id is rejected — run panels separately role lineage, functional, technical, viability, barcode, other use_for_clustering, use_for_correction, use_for_evaluation three independent masks

The three masks are independent on purpose. Clustering a correction backend does internally is a different thing from the evaluation markers, and neither is automatically the correction scope.

docs.title: processing.json
docs.text:
{
  "compensated": true, "unmixed": false,
  "compensation_source": "acquisition-time spillover matrix",
  "qc_history": ["PeacoQC v1.2 upstream of this workflow"],
  "transformation": "asinh", "transformation_parameters": {"cofactor": 5.0},
  "scale": "asinh_cofactor5", "units": "arcsinh units", "corrected": false
}

scale is mandatory. corrected: true is refused: the input is the uncorrected baseline, and chained correction is not supported by default. There is no universal cofactor — declare it per panel, and do not apply spectral-flow defaults to CyTOF. The community conventions from the cyCombine paper are cofactor 5 for CyTOF, 150 for conventional flow and 6000 for spectral flow; they are conventions, not defaults, so declare the value that matches the instrument and panel. A scale of the form asinh_cofactor<N> must agree with transformation_parameters.cofactor; a disagreement is rejected at load time.

docs.title: 3. Configuring a run
docs.text:
config/README.md lists three shipped configurations; batchdx-cyto init materialises any of them with its data. Validation is strict and unknown keys are rejected:

batchdx-cyto validate --config config/config.yaml

Validation refuses three different things, and the difference matters. An unknown key is a typo. A removed key is one this build used to accept and then never read, so setting it produced a run that looked configured and was not; preprocessing.time_channel is the only one in that category now, and validate names it and says what to use instead. A refused value is a key that stays but cannot take every value: evaluation.sampling.unit is sample_id and nothing else, evaluation.representation.scaling is none, and report.offline is true, because this build has exactly one sampler, one coordinate system and one offline renderer. A key is never accepted at a value the package does not honour.

preprocessing.gating and preprocessing.peacoqc were in the removed category until 2026-09-30 and are now live keys, read as paths: to a gate table and to a PeacoQC settings file, both in the shape the pinned reference implementation's own configuration files declare. They are read by batchdx.cyto.preprocess, which runs as the pipeline's first stage when FCS input is used: gates on the raw events, per-panel asinh with the declared cofactors, then the PeacoQC pass on the transformed values — and a sample whose QC pass keeps fewer than half its events is refused rather than frozen into the baseline. The survivors are frozen into the baseline h5ad with per-event provenance (the original_event_index chain), and the design audit reads the preprocessed manifest. preprocessing.transformation no longer offers "logicle": this build implements no logicle, has no tested inverse for one, and the reference implementation contains none either.

docs.title: Reference requirements, by capability
docs.text: Capability Needs descriptive diagnosis nothing beyond a batch column drift diagnostic an acquisition axis: the FCS Time channel (ingested as acquisition_time) when present, otherwise the event index composition diagnostic frozen labels and ≥ 2 samples per batch reference_supported evidence a measured reference id shared by both batches of the pair cyCombine cluster detector 3–30 batches (upstream restriction, quoted in the eligibility manifest) CytoBatchFlagR a control sample in every batch, and ≥ 4 batches CytoNorm (strongest tier) a measured reference in every batch CytoNorm (control-free tier) nothing beyond ≥ 2 batches; weaker evidence (CytoNorm 2.0 QuantileNorm.train goal="mean" or a manual goal distribution)

docs.title: Confounding
docs.text:
If every batch contains exactly one level of a protected factor, the batch term and the factor term span the same subspace and neither is estimable. The audit marks the comparison non_identifiable, marks the cycombine backend ineligible with reason_code: batch_not_identifiable, and marks that entry non-overridable. An exploratory override exists (design.allow_exploratory_override) for eligibility failures that are a matter of judgement; it does not apply to a contrast that is arithmetically unavailable.

Adding the confounded factor as a covariate does not help. The report says so.

docs.title: The design floor
docs.text: design.minimum_batches (default 3) and design.require_shared_reference (default true). Both are configuration values with a declared origin, echoed into design_audit.json as design_floor_origin — not hidden constants. Below the floor every candidate is below_design_floor and the system produces descriptive output only.

docs.title: 4. Running
docs.text:
batchdx-cyto diagnose  --config config/config.yaml --outdir results/run1   # no correction
batchdx-cyto benchmark --config config/config.yaml --outdir results/run1   # all candidates
batchdx-cyto correct   --config config/config.yaml --outdir results/run1 --candidate cycombine_default
batchdx-cyto report    --config config/config.yaml --outdir results/run1   # re-render only

correct requires --candidate. There is no default and no automatic choice.

Every command delegates to Snakemake; README.md shows the equivalent native invocation. Pass --cores to control parallelism. A Snakemake profile (workflow/profiles/local/config.yaml, or the untested workflow/profiles/slurm/config.yaml) applies to the native invocation: the command-line wrapper has no --profile flag, because a profile rewrites scheduler and resource behaviour and a wrapper that hid that would be a wrapper you could not see through.

docs.title: 5. Reading the output
docs.text:
results/run1/
  config.resolved.json        resolved configuration + analytical fingerprint + versions
  manifests/                  dataset manifest, sampling manifest, exported JSON Schemas
  design/design_audit.json    contingency, rank, comparisons, eligibility
  diagnostics/<detector>/     detector_result.json, plots, native tables
  candidates/<id>/            correction_result.json, corrected.h5ad
  metrics/<id>/               metric_result.json
  decisions/                  decision_result.json
  status/run_status.json      one entry per planned unit, with its reason
  report/report.html          the offline report

docs.title: Interpreting metric records
docs.text:
Every record carries its namespace, direction, scale, status, coverage, aggregation weight, the label tier and confidence, and the five representation settings (space, marker mask, scaling, distance, k). Three things follow:

  • Namespace matters. native numbers come from upstream running its own partitioning (including cyCombine's moving uncorrected baseline). common numbers come from the one frozen partition. They are not interchangeable and a lower common EMD is not a better native score.
  • Status matters more than value. insufficient_data, undefined and ineligible are distinct, all carry a reason, and none is a zero.
  • label_tier: clustering is a caveat, not a footnote. Those labels came from the uncorrected data whose batch structure is under test.

docs.title: Interpreting the decision
docs.text:
not_needed, eligible_for_review, recommended_under_policy, rejected_distortion, insufficient_evidence, non_identifiable, below_design_floor, execution_failed.

The shipped policies use uncalibrated thresholds, and the report says so. A candidate that clears every gate under an uncalibrated policy reaches eligible_for_review, never recommended_under_policy. That is deliberate: these are engineering defaults, not validated universal cutoffs, and they must not be cited as such. To get automatic approval you must supply a policy whose threshold_origins state a real calibration — which means doing the calibration.

Retaining the uncorrected data is always an available outcome.

docs.title: Calibration, if you want it
docs.text: There is no calibration in this build. Calibrating means: choose a design like yours, establish ground truth (measured technical replicates are the only strong form), sweep min_emd_reduction, max_mad_compression_fraction and max_joint_structure_change, and record what error rate each choice buys you. Then declare that in threshold_origins. Until then, review.

docs.title: 6. Failure recovery
docs.text:
• A scientific skip is not a workflow failure. An ineligible or unavailable method produces a result file with a status and a reason, the run succeeds, and the report shows it under "Failures and limitations".
  • A genuine runtime failure keeps failure status; nothing is suppressed with || true or a blanket except.
  • Snakemake reruns what is missing. Deleting metrics/<id>/metric_result.json and decisions/decision_result.json forces both to be recomputed, because decide declares the metric files as real inputs rather than depending on a sentinel.
  • Changing a scientifically material setting changes the analytical fingerprint. Changing the report title does not.

docs.title: 7. Memory and scale
docs.text:
correct holds all relevant cells jointly for cyCombine: ComBat is fitted per SOM node across the whole dataset, so correcting files independently is not equivalent and chunking does not make it out-of-core. Size resources.mem_mb for the full matrix. Metrics and diagnostics are memory-bounded per group and parallelise across candidates.

No production-scale performance claim is made. The largest thing exercised in this build is a synthetic fixture of a few tens of thousands of cells.

docs.title: 8. Privacy
docs.text:
report.redact_identifiers is on by default: sample, donor and reference identifiers in the report become stable pseudonyms. The pseudonym mapping goes to report/identifier_map.json, deliberately a separate file, so a report can be circulated without it.

Identifiers are redacted. Paths are redacted too, on a stated rule. A path inside the project becomes <run>/…; a path outside it becomes <redacted>/<file name>, so the reader learns which file was read and not where it lives. This covers the resolved configuration the page prints, and the free-form payload each detector records for itself — its parameters, requirements, table and plot names, and warnings. A detector's parameters can carry one entry per evaluation cell (the pinned cycombine_express API groups by a column literally named sample, so a per-cell sample vector crosses the boundary), and a list longer than eight entries is replaced by its length and its first entries, with the page saying so.

Two limits, both stated on the page rather than here. A path inside a captured log line is not rewritten, because rewriting a log would falsify it — read such a warning as the machine's own text. And the dataset manifest's provenance is not rendered at all: only dataset_id reaches the page.

docs.title: 9. Extending
docs.text:
• A correction backend implements the CorrectionBackend protocol (adapters/base.py): declare BackendCapabilities honestly — especially supports_fit_apply and fit_apply_verified — then register_backend. Unsupported parameters must go in rejected_parameters with a reason.
  • A detector implements the Detector protocol (diagnostics/base.py) and returns a DetectorResult for a scientific skip rather than raising.
  • A metric registers a MetricSpec (metrics/registry.py). Use the common namespace unless you have verified your implementation against a pinned upstream one; scripts/audit_upstream.py fails the build if anything claims compatibility without upstream_verified.
  • Adding an R call means adding it to adapter_calls in config/upstream_lock.yaml, or the Stage 0 test will fail — by design, so no adapter can quietly grow a call the audit never checks. That gate is test_r_audit_runs_and_finds_every_adapter_referenced_function in tests/integration/test_stage0_audit.py, and it skips when no R interpreter is on PATH; on a machine without R, adding an adapter call is not caught. Run the R environment before relying on it.

docs.title: 10. Known limits
docs.text: Read docs/implementation_status.md (generated) and docs/blocked.md before relying on anything. In short: the R backends execute for real at their pinned versions and CI builds the full R environment, but they remain the least exercised paths; the biological-preservation metrics are implemented with donor-paired uncertainty, yet no candidate has been shown to preserve biology on a real cohort; the OpenProblems metrics are partially verified and partially deferred; there is no real-data example; and no clinical or unseen-batch generalisation claim is made.

docs.title: Validation results
docs.text:
What the scientific suite establishes, and — more importantly — what it does not.

docs/implementation_status.md is generated from an executed test report and is the authority on which gates passed. This file explains what those tests mean.

docs.title: The fixtures
docs.text:
All of it runs on deterministic synthetic data from batchdx.cyto.simulate. Five populations with declared marker means, a shared per-cell latent factor within each population (so markers genuinely co-vary, which is what makes a joint-structure metric measurable at all), and separately controllable perturbations:

Knob Injects batch_shift a technical offset per batch and marker batch_spread a technical dispersion change group_shift a genuine biological difference drift a within-file trend across acquisition order per-sample frequencies a composition difference within_population_correlation co-expression structure to preserve or destroy

These are fixtures, not a scientific claim. Public spectral controls have been obtained and audited, but no real-data correction has run. Nothing here demonstrates behaviour on real data. This Alpha ships no real cytometry data or real-data example — see item 4 below and examples/README.md, where the same statement sits on the face of the documentation rather than only in a blocked-items file.

docs.title: Validation-only backends
docs.text:
tests/fixtures/backends.py registers three controls that are not user correction methods and are deliberately not registered by the package:

  • fixture_offset_removal — the correct answer for the paired-reference fixture: subtract each batch's offset as measured on its reference aliquot.
  • fixture_collapse — replaces every value with the population's median across all batches. Alignment becomes perfect; all spread is destroyed.
  • fixture_joint_scramble — permutes each marker independently within each (population, batch) group. Every marginal is preserved exactly; co-expression is destroyed.
  • fixture_failure — always raises, to exercise the failure path.

docs.title: Metrics respond to what they claim to measure
docs.text:
• Identical distributions give near-zero EMD; a known translation moves it.
  • A pure scale change shows up in mad_signed_change as a negative value. The cyCombine MAD score takes an absolute difference and cannot tell restoration from compression, which is why the signed metric exists under a different name.
  • A constant marker gives undefined, never zero.
  • A rare population gives insufficient_data with the required cell count in the reason.
  • A near-zero denominator gives undefined; no epsilon is applied.
  • median_abs_deviation(scale="normal") reproduces the 1.4826 consistency constant, so the dispersion metric is on the same footing as R's stats::mad.

docs.title: Composition is separable from intensity
docs.text: Dropping 80 % of one population's cells from one batch's evaluation set moves the composition metric by more than 0.05 while every within-population EMD for the other populations moves by less than 1e-9. A frequency shift cannot masquerade as an intensity artefact.

docs.title: The joint-structure metric earns its place
docs.text: fixture_joint_scramble leaves every EMD and every MAD unchanged to within 1e-9, and the joint-structure metric still detects it. Without that row, a corruption that preserves all marginals while destroying co-expression would be invisible — which is precisely the Stage 8 requirement.

docs.title: Guardrails reject destructive corrections
docs.text: fixture_collapse achieves better alignment than the baseline and is rejected (rejected_distortion), because the compression guardrail fires. A system that rewarded alignment alone would recommend it.

docs.title: The design audit refuses unsupportable claims
docs.text: Perfect confounding yields non_identifiable, marks the cyCombine backend ineligible with reason_code: batch_not_identifiable, and marks that entry non-overridable. A purely biological shift present in every batch does not inflate batch-pair EMD.

docs.title: Upstream constraints are derived, not asserted
docs.text: The four-batch minimum for CytoBatchFlagR is proven arithmetically: over 2000 random draws of three values, the 1.5 IQR Tukey fence is never exceeded, and a four-value counterexample is shown. The 3–30 batch range for cyCombine's cluster detector is read from the pinned source and quoted in the eligibility reason.

docs.title: Abstention works
docs.text: Uncalibrated thresholds produce eligible_for_review, never recommended_under_policy. A policy whose threshold_origins state a real calibration can recommend — tested — which shows the gate is a gate and not a permanent refusal. Removing a candidate's own failing guardrail metric does not promote it.

docs.title: What these tests do NOT establish
docs.text:
Stated plainly, because the absence of a test is not evidence of correctness:

  1. Biological preservation is demonstrated on synthetic fixtures only. Stage 8 is now implemented: prespecified contrasts, paired and unpaired sample-level models, donor-block bootstrap, restricted permutation, and an uncertainty interval on every emitted record. But the fixtures are deterministic and synthetic, so this establishes that the machinery detects, refuses and quantifies correctly — it is not a calibration for any real cohort, and no threshold in it should be cited as one. The single most important limit on this package is that it has never seen real cytometry data (item 4).
  2. Both correction backends and the CytoBatchFlagR detector execute. cyCombine 0.3.0 and CytoNorm 2.0.12 run at their pinned commits; CytoBatchFlagR's detector executes against a four-batch fixture and distinguishes its injected shift from the corresponding unshifted design. Its 1.5-IQR flag remains uncalibrated for multiple tests, so a flag is not a validated false-positive-controlled decision. CytoNorm only normalises batches with a fitted control; the result reports the samples it left unchanged. See docs/blocked.md B-005 and B-006.
  3. Seven upstream metric components are verified; two metric names are not. Seven of the OpenProblems components at commit 37151479 are registered in the compatibility namespace with upstream_verified=True, each proven by a test that imports the pinned helper file and compares outputs on a shared fixture at the tolerances tabulated below: emd_mean_ct_horiz, emd_mean_ct_vert, ratio_consistent_peaks, average_batch_r2_ct, iLisi, cLisi and flowsom_mean_mapping_similarity. Extraction did not need the Nextflow runtime. What is not verified is the case-assembly loop in the components' script.py / script.R files, which read .h5ad resources the pinned checkout does not carry; those loops are documented transcriptions with the classifier tested directly, and for the FlowSOM component the three benchmark parameters the pinned script reads from the data are declared constants on the spec instead. The remaining two names are in DEFERRED_METRICS with a currently-true obstacle, and openproblems.cms is recorded as genuinely absent at the pinned commit. The audit script fails the build if anything claims compatibility without verification.
  4. No real-data validation yet. Behaviour on heavy tails, multimodality, marker dropout, instrument artefacts and genuine spillover is untested, and every scientific result here rests on batchdx.cyto.simulate. A public spectral-control dataset is downloaded outside Git, with a 24-file homogeneous subset audited, but its correction endpoints have not been run (docs/blocked.md B-008). The 0.1.0 Alpha ships no real cytometry data or real-data example. Read any number in this file as a property of the code on synthetic input, not as a calibration for any cohort. The same statement is on the face of examples/README.md, docs/compatibility_matrix.md and README.md.
  5. Multi-seed, but only over the claims that can be checked across seeds. tests/scientific/test_multiseed.py runs 25 tests over five seeds (473, 7, 101, 20250930, 65537), and it holds at every one of them: a correct offset removal reduces alignment error on both shifted markers; a metric recomputed on the same data is bit-identical; the same seed reproduces both the data and the frozen evaluation draw; different seeds produce different data and different draws; a confounded design is non_identifiable and recommends nothing; and a calibrated policy can still recommend on the reference-supported design, so the refusal above is the design and not a permanently closed gate. The seeds also caught a real defect: the shipped examples wrote a configuration declaring seed: 473 regardless of the seed their data was generated with, so materialise_example(..., seed=7) shipped data and a run record that disagreed.

What this is not. It is not a five-seed re-run of the scientific suite. It cannot be one: the existing scientific tests take their data from the frozen fixture in tests/conftest.py, which calls materialise_example without a seed, so their data is 473 whatever a parametrisation says. The cost is not the obstacle either — tests/scientific takes 1m47s, so five passes would be under ten minutes. Making it a genuine suite-wide sweep needs a seed-aware conftest, which is a change to a shared file and therefore a central change, not something the sweep can do for itself. Until that lands, Stage 7 metrics, Stage 8 preservation and Stage 9 decisions remain single-seed, and this file says so rather than letting a passing 25-test file imply otherwise. 6. No cluster execution. The SLURM profile has never run on a cluster and says so. The container has never been built. 7. No calibration. Every recommendation threshold is an uncalibrated engineering default. They are not validated cutoffs and must not be cited as such. 8. No performance claim. The largest thing exercised is a few tens of thousands of synthetic cells.

docs.title: Tolerances used
docs.text:
Check Tolerance Why marginal preservation under scrambling 1e-9 the permutation is exact; anything larger would be a bug excluded-marker invariance 1e-9 (INVARIANCE_ATOL) backends run in float64; larger is a real modification identical-distribution EMD < 1e-3 sampling noise on ~1e3 cells per group offset removal on affected markers after < 0.5 × before the offset is 0.6–0.8 on a spread of 0.35 collapse compression fraction > 0.9 collapse destroys spread in essentially every group joint-structure change under scrambling > 0.1 rho² = 0.36 co-expression is removed pinned emd/helper.py:bin_array exact (np.array_equal) pure np.histogram; any difference is a porting error, not sampling noise pinned emd/helper.py:compute_emd, per marker < 1e-9 relative a weighted wasserstein_distance over a fixed 2000-bin grid; only float summation order can differ pinned emd/helper.py horizontal and vertical means < 1e-9 relative the same distances, pooled over more markers in a different order pinned ratio_consistent_peaks/helper.py density and peak count < 1e-12 absolute, exact counts pure gaussian_kde and find_peaks; deterministic, so the bar is the port being correct pinned average_batch_r2/helper.py, per marker and aggregate < 1e-9 relative measured agreement 2e-16. Only correct once one dummy is fitted per batch; a single 0/1 contrast is a different model and a test asserts the two differ by more than 0.05 pinned lisi/helper.py per-cell iLisi and cLisi exact (rtol=0, atol=0) pynndescent is deterministic at the pinned seed, so per-cell parity is achievable rather than merely statistical; the normalisation is compared at 1e-12 relative CytoNorm FCS round trip to the float32 storage bound FCS stores float32, so a round trip is not bit-exact and the bound is measured (FCS_STORAGE_DTYPE, round_trip_tolerance) rather than assumed CytoNorm correction magnitude, injected marker vs others affected marker > 0.4 mean absolute; others ≤ 0.05 only CD4 carries an injected offset on the fixture, so a correction that moved every marker would be a red flag rather than a success

These are predeclared in the tests. They were not loosened to obtain a favourable result; where a test initially failed, the cause was a fixture that did not contain the structure being tested for (no co-expression to destroy; a collapse that did not actually align), and the fixture was corrected, not the tolerance.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The package lives at batchdx.cyto. The public surface is organised by stage: input and manifests (io), preprocessing (preprocess), the design audit (design), diagnostics (diagnostics), correction backends (adapters), the frozen sampling layer (sampling), metrics (metrics), the decision layer (decisions), the report (reporting), and the schemas every stage exchanges (schemas).

Every stage boundary is a contract: the schemas module defines what one stage may hand to another, and the contracts are enforced, not conventional. Start with schemas if you want to understand the data model, or with pipeline if you want to see the stages in order.

docs.title: BackendIneligible
docs.text:
Bases: BackendError

The backend is installed and works, but this design cannot support a fit.

A design-coverage refusal is a statement about the DATA, not about the installation: "no measured reference falls in the training split" and "the frozen partition is not arm-balanced" are properties of the dataset and the split, and they resolve by declaring more biospecimens or re-partitioning -- never by installing a package. A missing R package is :class:BackendNotAvailable, an environment fact that resolves by installing it.

The two are distinct exception types, not message conventions, because substring matching on the message cannot make the distinction: any real failure whose text happens to mention a training split would be recorded as a coverage gap, which is how a genuine defect gets recorded as a data limitation.

docs.title: BackendNotAvailable
docs.text:
Bases: BackendError

The backend is absent or unusable in this environment, rather than broken.

This is a distinct type, not a message convention, because docs/decisions/0006-candidate-results-and-failure-handling.md requires not_available and failed to stay distinguishable. The two mean different things to a reader of a report: "this method was not installed here" is an environment fact that resolves by installing it, while "this method ran and broke" is a statement about the method. A backend that raises BackendError is recorded as failed; only this subclass is recorded as not_available.

Substring matching on the message cannot make that distinction: any real failure whose text happens to mention a missing package would be reported as a missing package, which is how a genuine defect gets recorded as an environment gap.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/adapters/base.py

    This is a distinct type, not a message convention, because

    status: CorrectionStatus,

    software: list[SoftwareVersion] | None = None,
) -> CorrectionResult:
    """A failed or ineligible candidate, with no output path and no fabricated values."""

    return CorrectionResult(
        candidate=spec, status=status, reason=reason, software=software or [],
        validation={"produced_output": False},
    )

docs.text:
Merge requested parameters onto the pinned defaults, rejecting anything unsupported.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/adapters/base.py 
def resolve_parameters(
    capabilities: BackendCapabilities, requested: dict[str, Any]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Merge requested parameters onto the pinned defaults, rejecting anything unsupported."""

    refused = [k for k in requested if k in capabilities.rejected_parameters]
    if refused:
        details = "; ".join(f"{k}: {capabilities.rejected_parameters[k]}" for k in refused)
        raise BackendError(f"backend {capabilities.name!r} refuses parameter(s) {refused}. {details}")
    unknown = [
        k for k in requested
        if k not in capabilities.accepted_parameters and k not in capabilities.rejected_parameters
    ]
    if unknown:
        raise BackendError(
            f"backend {capabilities.name!r} does not accept parameter(s) {unknown}; "
            f"accepted parameters are {sorted(capabilities.accepted_parameters)}"
        )
    resolved = dict(capabilities.accepted_parameters)
    resolved.update(requested)
    return resolved

@app.command()
def audit(
    out_dir: Path = typer.Option(Path("docs/audit"), help="Where to write the audit artifacts."),
    upstream_dir: Path = typer.Option(
        Path(".upstream"), help="Directory holding the pinned upstream checkouts."
    ),
    rscript: str = typer.Option("Rscript"),
) -> None:
    """Run the Stage 0 upstream audit scripts and store their captured output."""

    # Resolve the audit scripts from the installed package first (the wheel ships
    # them under workflow_assets via hatch force-include), then from the repo
    # layout so an editable checkout keeps working.
    packaged = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "workflow_assets" / "scripts"
    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts"
    scripts_dir = packaged if (packaged / "audit_upstream.py").exists() else repo
    py_script = scripts_dir / "audit_upstream.py"
    r_script = scripts_dir / "audit_upstream.R"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    failures = []
    if py_script.exists():
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(py_script), "--out", str(out_dir / "audit_python.json"),
             "--upstream-dir", str(upstream_dir)],
            check=False,
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            failures.append("audit_upstream.py")
    else:
        failures.append(f"{py_script} not found")

    if shutil.which(rscript) and r_script.exists():
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [rscript, "--vanilla", str(r_script), str(out_dir / "audit_r.json"),
             str(upstream_dir)],
            check=False,
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            failures.append("audit_upstream.R")
    else:
        typer.secho(
            f"skipping the R audit: {rscript!r} not on PATH or {r_script} missing",
            fg=typer.colors.YELLOW, err=True,
        )

    if failures:
        _fail("audit failed for: " + ", ".join(failures), code=4)
    typer.secho(f"audit artifacts written to {out_dir}", fg=typer.colors.GREEN)

docs.title: batchdx.cyto.config
docs.text:
Strict configuration schema (schema_version: 2).

Unknown keys are rejected everywhere. So are keys this build cannot honour, in two distinct ways, because a configuration that is accepted and then ignored is the worst outcome available: the run looks configured and is not.

  • :data:UNSUPPORTED_KEYS names keys this build removed entirely. Setting one is refused with the reason and the thing to use instead.
  • :data:SUPPORTED_VALUES names keys that stay, but only for the values the package can actually deliver. Any other value is refused by name rather than accepted and dropped on the floor. Where a key has exactly one meaningful value the schema pins it, so the key records an invariant instead of advertising a choice that does not exist.

tests/unit/test_config_keys.py walks every model below and fails the build if a leaf is neither read by a non-schema module nor listed, with a justification, in the test's DECLARATIVE_ONLY allow-list. That test is what stops this drifting back.

Backend parameters left unspecified are resolved to the pinned documented defaults recorded in :mod:batchdx.cyto.adapters and serialised into the resolved configuration, so a run never depends on an upstream default silently changing.

docs.title: PreprocessingConfig
docs.text:
Bases: _Strict

A declaration about the data, and — since Tranche 3 — a declaration of the upstream step that produced it.

enabled and transformation are read exactly once, to refuse a configuration that claims a transformation the processing manifest contradicts, and cofactor_by_panel is read by batchdx.cyto.pipeline.stage_preprocess, which applies the per-panel cofactors to raw events when this run, and not an upstream step, performs the preprocessing. When the stage runs, the frozen baseline it writes is already transformed, and the derived configuration every later stage loads declares no further transformation -- _validate_processing in io.dataset refuses a run that would transform twice.

gating and peacoqc are paths to the upstream step's own declaration, not instructions to this run. They are read by :func:batchdx.cyto.preprocess.gating.gates_from_config and :func:batchdx.cyto.preprocess.peacoqc.settings_from_config, which apply the gate table and run PeacoQC over the raw events before a baseline exists. A run that never calls those functions ignores them, exactly as it ignores cofactor_by_panel; that is stated here so the key is not mistaken for a switch the correction workflow reads.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/config.py 
class PreprocessingConfig(_Strict):
    """A declaration about the data, and — since Tranche 3 — a declaration of the
    upstream step that produced it.

    ``enabled`` and ``transformation`` are read exactly once, to refuse a configuration
    that claims a transformation the processing manifest contradicts, and
    ``cofactor_by_panel`` is read by ``batchdx.cyto.pipeline.stage_preprocess``, which
    applies the per-panel cofactors to raw events when this run, and not an upstream
    step, performs the preprocessing.  When the stage runs, the frozen baseline it
    writes is already transformed, and the derived configuration every later stage
    loads declares no further transformation -- ``_validate_processing`` in
    ``io.dataset`` refuses a run that would transform twice.

    ``gating`` and ``peacoqc`` are **paths to the upstream step's own declaration**, not
    instructions to this run.  They are read by
    :func:`batchdx.cyto.preprocess.gating.gates_from_config` and
    :func:`batchdx.cyto.preprocess.peacoqc.settings_from_config`, which apply the gate
    table and run PeacoQC over the raw events *before* a baseline exists.  A run that
    never calls those functions ignores them, exactly as it ignores
    ``cofactor_by_panel``; that is stated here so the key is not mistaken for a switch
    the correction workflow reads.
    """

    enabled: bool = False
    # "logicle" was removed from this Literal on 2026-09-30.  It was a declaration, not a
    # capability: this build implements no logicle, io/export.py has no tested inverse
    # for one, and the pinned reference implementation contains none either
    # (`grep -i logicle` over .upstream/spiscy returns zero matches).  Accepting it
    # validated a value and bought nothing, which is exactly the accepted-and-ignored
    # failure this module exists to prevent.  preprocess.transform.LOGICLE keeps the
    # refusal reason reachable in code.
    transformation: Literal["asinh", "none"] | None = None
    #: Declared per-panel cofactors.  Applied to raw events by
    #: ``batchdx.cyto.pipeline.stage_preprocess`` when this run performs the
    #: preprocessing; the cofactor that the FCS exporter inverts is still the one in
    #: the processing manifest of the values a run actually reads.
    cofactor_by_panel: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    #: Path to a two-dimensional gate table in the reference implementation's YAML
    #: shape.  ``None`` means no gate is declared, which is a statement about the
    #: upstream step, not an instruction to skip one that exists.
    gating: str | None = None
    #: Path to a PeacoQC settings file.  ``None`` means no PeacoQC pass is declared.
    peacoqc: str | None = None

    @field_validator("gating", "peacoqc")
    @classmethod
    def _a_declared_path_is_a_path(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Refuse a blank path rather than accept one that resolves to nothing.

        ``gating: ""`` would otherwise validate and then name a directory. An empty
        string is not "no gate"; it is a path to the current working directory, and
        reading a gate table from there is not what anyone meant.
        """

        if v is not None and not str(v).strip():
            raise ValueError(
                "this key names a file. An empty string is a path to the current working "
                "directory, not an absence: leave the key out entirely to declare that "
                "there is no such step"
            )
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _require_declared_cofactor(self) -> PreprocessingConfig:
        if self.enabled and self.transformation == "asinh" and not self.cofactor_by_panel:
            raise ValueError(
                "preprocessing.transformation: 'asinh' requires "
                "preprocessing.cofactor_by_panel; there is no universal cofactor"
            )
        return self

class BiologicalContrastConfig(_Strict):
    """One prespecified biological contrast that correction must not destroy.

    A contrast is a difference between two levels of a sample-level factor (usually
    the biological ``group``) on one declared marker.  The tolerance is the maximum
    change in that difference a candidate may cause for the contrast to count as
    preserved.  Both the tolerance and *where it came from* are configuration: a
    tolerance without a declared origin is rejected, because an unexplained cutoff is
    not a predeclared tolerance.
    """

    contrast_id: str
    marker: str
    group_a: str
    group_b: str
    #: Sample-level factor whose levels ``group_a``/``group_b`` are.  Must resolve on
    #: the sample manifest; ``group`` is the usual choice.
    group_factor: str = "group"
    #: Maximum tolerated change in the contrast's effect size (in units of the declared
    #: expression scale), after correction relative to before.
    preservation_tolerance: float
    #: Declared origin of ``preservation_tolerance`` (e.g. a preanalysis document, a
    #: published minimal clinically important difference, or an explicit pilot).
    preservation_tolerance_origin: str

    @field_validator("preservation_tolerance")
    @classmethod
    def _positive_tolerance(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if v <= 0:
            raise ValueError("preservation_tolerance must be strictly positive")
        return v

    @field_validator("preservation_tolerance_origin")
    @classmethod
    def _origin_declared(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if not v.strip():
            raise ValueError(
                "preservation_tolerance_origin must name where the tolerance comes from; "
                "a threshold without a declared origin is not predeclared"
            )
        return v

class Config(_Strict):
    schema_version: int
    project: ProjectConfig
    input: InputConfig
    preprocessing: PreprocessingConfig = Field(default_factory=PreprocessingConfig)
    design: DesignConfig
    evaluation: EvaluationConfig
    correction: CorrectionConfig
    detectors: DetectorsConfig = Field(default_factory=DetectorsConfig)
    upstream: UpstreamConfig = Field(default_factory=UpstreamConfig)
    report: ReportConfig = Field(default_factory=ReportConfig)
    exports: ExportsConfig = Field(default_factory=ExportsConfig)

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _refuse_removed_keys(cls, raw: Any) -> Any:
        """Name a key this build removed, rather than reporting it as unknown."""

        if isinstance(raw, dict):
            for dotted, why in UNSUPPORTED_KEYS.items():
                section, _, leaf = dotted.partition(".")
                block = raw.get(section)
                if isinstance(block, dict) and leaf in block:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{dotted}: this build does not support this key, because {why}. "
                        f"It was removed rather than left accepted-and-ignored."
                    )
        return raw

    @field_validator("schema_version")
    @classmethod
    def _check_version(cls, v: int) -> int:
        if v != CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(
                f"schema_version {v} is not supported; this build reads "
                f"schema_version {CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION}"
            )
        return v

    # -- analytical identity ---------------------------------------------------------

    def analytical_fingerprint(self) -> str:
        """Hash of the scientifically material settings only.

        Cosmetic reporting settings are excluded so that changing a report title does
        not invalidate correction outputs.
        """
        payload = self.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"report"})
        return hashlib.sha256(
            json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
        ).hexdigest()

    def resolved_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self.model_dump(mode="json")

    Cosmetic reporting settings are excluded so that changing a report title does
    not invalidate correction outputs.
    """
    payload = self.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"report"})
    return hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
    ).hexdigest()

def load_config(path: str | Path) -> Config:
    """Read and strictly validate a configuration file."""

    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        raise ConfigError(f"configuration file not found: {p}")
    try:
        raw = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - passthrough
        raise ConfigError(f"{p}: not valid YAML: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise ConfigError(f"{p}: top level of the configuration must be a mapping")
    return parse_config(raw, source=str(p))

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    """A named, publishable set of gates."""

    name: str
    min_coverage: float = 0.6
    min_emd_reduction: float = 0.2
    max_mad_compression_fraction: float = 0.25
    max_joint_structure_change: float = 0.1
    #: EMD below which the identity candidate is taken to show no batch effect worth
    #: correcting.  Uncalibrated.
    no_effect_emd: float = 0.05
    require_reference_supported: bool = True
    threshold_origins: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {
        "min_coverage": "uncalibrated engineering default",
        "min_emd_reduction": "uncalibrated engineering default",
        "max_mad_compression_fraction": "uncalibrated engineering default",
        "max_joint_structure_change": "uncalibrated engineering default",
        "no_effect_emd": "uncalibrated engineering default",
    })
    #: Per-threshold calibration evidence: threshold name -> reference to a calibration
    #: artifact (path, URI or hash).  Origins are self-declared and the artifact is not
    #: re-verified here, but a policy that declares itself calibrated must at least name
    #: what it was calibrated against, for every threshold, by construction.
    calibration_artifacts: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def any_threshold_uncalibrated(self) -> bool:
        for name, origin in self.threshold_origins.items():
            if "uncalibrated" in origin:
                return True
            if not self.calibration_artifacts.get(name):
                # An origin that merely avoids the word "uncalibrated" is not
                # calibration evidence; a calibrated policy must name its artifact.
                return True
        return False
