docs.text:
The extracted OpenProblems components, on the frozen common partition.

design is accepted for signature parity with :func:compute_common_metrics. The extracted components group by donor, sample and batch and never by a declared batch pair, so nothing here reads it. rscript and work_dir are the FlowSOM component's R side: the interpreter to call and where the binary matrices and logs for the (reference, mapped) pairs go.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/openproblems.py 
def compute_openproblems_metrics(
    dataset: Dataset,
    candidate_matrix: np.ndarray,
    sampling: SamplingManifest,
    design: DesignAudit,
    *,
    run_id: str,
    candidate_id: str,
    rscript: str = "Rscript",
    work_dir: Path | None = None,
) -> MetricResult:
    """The extracted OpenProblems components, on the frozen common partition.

    ``design`` is accepted for signature parity with :func:`compute_common_metrics`.  The
    extracted components group by donor, sample and batch and never by a declared batch
    pair, so nothing here reads it.  ``rscript`` and ``work_dir`` are the FlowSOM
    component's R side: the interpreter to call and where the binary matrices and logs
    for the (reference, mapped) pairs go.
    """

    if not sampling.evaluation_markers:
        return MetricResult(
            run_id=run_id, candidate_id=candidate_id, metric_group="openproblems",
            status="ineligible",
            reason="no marker is flagged use_for_evaluation in the marker manifest",
        )

    panel = _panel(dataset, sampling)
    candidate = _candidate_panel(panel, dataset, candidate_matrix)
    records: list[MetricRecord] = []
    records += _horizontal_emd(panel, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _vertical_emd(panel, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _ratio_consistent_peaks(panel, candidate, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _residual_batch_r2(panel, candidate, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _ilisi(panel, candidate, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _clisi(panel, candidate, sampling, run_id, candidate_id)
    records += _flowsom_records(
        panel, candidate, sampling, run_id, candidate_id,
        rscript=rscript, work_dir=work_dir,
    )

    n_failed = sum(1 for r in records if r.status is MetricStatus.FAILED)
    return MetricResult(
        run_id=run_id, candidate_id=candidate_id, metric_group="openproblems",
        records=records, status="ok" if not n_failed else "partial",
    )

docs.title: compute_preservation_metrics(dataset, candidate_matrix, sampling, design, contrasts, *, run_id, candidate_id)
docs.text:
Biological preservation for one candidate, on the frozen partition.

A refused contrast becomes one biological_contrast_admissibility record carrying its reason, so a contrast that could not be run is visible in the record set instead of absent from it. Every record that reports a value also reports the interval and the method that produced it.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/preservation.py 
def compute_preservation_metrics(
    dataset: Dataset,
    candidate_matrix: np.ndarray,
    sampling: SamplingManifest,
    design: DesignAudit,
    contrasts: list[ContrastSpec],
    *,
    run_id: str,
    candidate_id: str,
) -> MetricResult:
    """Biological preservation for one candidate, on the frozen partition.

    A refused contrast becomes one ``biological_contrast_admissibility`` record carrying
    its reason, so a contrast that could not be run is visible in the record set instead
    of absent from it.  Every record that reports a value also reports the interval and
    the method that produced it.
    """

    records: list[MetricRecord] = []
    frozen = _frozen_rows_by_sample(dataset, sampling)
    feature_idx = {str(name): i for i, name in enumerate(dataset.adata.var_names)}

    for spec in contrasts:
        outcome = resolve_contrast(dataset, design, sampling, spec)
        if isinstance(outcome, ContrastRefusal):
            records.append(_refusal_record(outcome, sampling, run_id, candidate_id))
            continue
        plan = outcome
        records.append(_admissible_record(plan, sampling, run_id, candidate_id))

        for population in plan.populations:
            by_sample = frozen.get(population, {})
            present = [sid for sid in plan.contributing if sid in by_sample]
            usable = [
                sid for sid in present if len(by_sample[sid]) >= MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE_MEAN
            ]
            scope = (
                f"population {population!r} contributes {len(usable)} of "
                f"{plan.n_samples} sample(s) with at least "
                f"{MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE_MEAN} frozen evaluation cells"
            )
            if len(present) < len(plan.contributing):
                scope += (
                    f"; {len(plan.contributing) - len(present)} carry no cell of this "
                    "population on the frozen partition"
                )
            if len(present) > len(usable):
                scope += f"; {len(present) - len(usable)} fell below that cell floor"
            n_cells = sum(len(by_sample[sid]) for sid in usable)
            coverage = len(usable) / plan.n_samples if plan.n_samples else 0.0
            for marker in plan.markers:
                column = feature_idx[marker]
                values = np.array(
                    [candidate_matrix[np.asarray(by_sample[sid], dtype=int), column].mean()
                     for sid in usable], dtype=float
                )
                matrix = donor_level_matrix(plan, usable, values)
                records.extend(_one_group(
                    matrix, plan, sampling, population, marker, run_id, candidate_id,
                    n_cells, coverage, scope,
                ))

    status = "ok" if all(
        r.status in (MetricStatus.OK, MetricStatus.INELIGIBLE,
                     MetricStatus.INSUFFICIENT_DATA, MetricStatus.UNDEFINED)
        for r in records
    ) else "partial"
    return MetricResult(
        run_id=run_id, candidate_id=candidate_id, metric_group="biological_preservation",
        records=records, status=status,
        reason=None if records else "no biological contrast was prespecified for this run",
    )

docs.title: resolve_contrast(dataset, design, sampling, spec)
docs.text:
Decide whether a prespecified contrast may be run, and with which replicate unit.

Every branch that refuses names the condition that failed. A contrast is never dropped without a record, and never reported as a score of zero.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/preservation.py 
def resolve_contrast(
    dataset: Dataset,
    design: DesignAudit,
    sampling: SamplingManifest,
    spec: ContrastSpec,
) -> ContrastPlan | ContrastRefusal:
    """Decide whether a prespecified contrast may be run, and with which replicate unit.

    Every branch that refuses names the condition that failed.  A contrast is never
    dropped without a record, and never reported as a score of zero.
    """

    values = _factor_values(dataset, spec.factor)
    levels_present = sorted({v for v in values.values() if v is not None})
    if not levels_present:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "unknown_factor",
            f"no sample declares {spec.factor!r}, so the contrast has no data to run on; "
            f"the declared levels were {spec.level_a!r} and {spec.level_b!r}",
        )

    missing = [lvl for lvl in (spec.level_a, spec.level_b) if lvl not in levels_present]
    if missing:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "levels_absent",
            f"level(s) {missing} of contrast {spec.contrast_id!r} are not present in "
            f"{spec.factor!r}; the sample table carries {levels_present}. A contrast is "
            "prespecified, not discovered after the fact.",
        )

    # -- identifiability ---------------------------------------------------------------
    if spec.factor not in design.protected_factors:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "factor_not_protected",
            f"{spec.factor!r} is not among the design's declared protected factors "
            f"{list(design.protected_factors)}, so a difference in it is not separately "
            "estimable from the batch effect; declare it in design.protect first",
        )
    if spec.factor in design.confounded_factors:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "non_identifiable",
            f"the design audit reports {spec.factor!r} perfectly confounded with "
            f"{design.correction_factor!r} (confounded_factors="
            f"{list(design.confounded_factors)}); the batch term and the {spec.factor!r} "
            "term span the same subspace, so no covariate adjustment separates them and no "
            "preservation claim can rest on this contrast",
        )
    batch_values = _factor_values(dataset, design.correction_factor)
    level_by_batch: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for sid, level in values.items():
        if level in {spec.level_a, spec.level_b} and batch_values.get(sid):
            level_by_batch.setdefault(str(batch_values[sid]), set()).add(str(level))
    if len(level_by_batch) > 1 and all(len(v) == 1 for v in level_by_batch.values()):
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "non_identifiable",
            f"the two levels of {spec.factor!r} occupy disjoint batches "
            f"({ {b: sorted(v)[0] for b, v in sorted(level_by_batch.items())} }); the "
            "biological contrast and the batch contrast are the same contrast",
        )

    # -- declared covariates -----------------------------------------------------------
    for covariate in spec.protected_covariates:
        covariate_values = _factor_values(dataset, covariate)
        present = {v for v in covariate_values.values() if v is not None}
        if not present:
            return ContrastRefusal(
                spec, "covariate_absent",
                f"protected covariate {covariate!r} is declared on this contrast but no "
                "sample carries it, so the contrast would not be conditional on anything",
            )
        if present <= {spec.level_a, spec.level_b}:
            return ContrastRefusal(
                spec, "covariate_nested_in_contrast",
                f"protected covariate {covariate!r} is nested inside {spec.factor!r}: its "
                f"levels {sorted(present)} are a subset of "
                f"{{{spec.level_a!r}, {spec.level_b!r}}}, so the contrast and the "
                "covariate cannot be separated",
            )

    # -- scope -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    evaluation_markers = tuple(sampling.evaluation_markers)
    markers = evaluation_markers if spec.markers is None else tuple(spec.markers)
    if not markers:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "no_evaluation_markers",
            "the frozen partition names no marker flagged use_for_evaluation, so there is "
            "nothing to test",
        )
    absent_markers = [m for m in markers if m not in evaluation_markers]
    if absent_markers:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "marker_absent",
            f"marker(s) {absent_markers} are not flagged use_for_evaluation on the frozen "
            f"partition, which carries {list(evaluation_markers)}",
        )
    frozen_populations = sorted(set(sampling.labels_by_cell.values()))
    populations = (
        tuple(frozen_populations) if spec.populations is None else tuple(spec.populations)
    )
    absent_populations = [p for p in populations if p not in frozen_populations]
    if not populations or absent_populations:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "population_absent",
            f"population(s) {absent_populations or list(populations)} are not on the frozen "
            f"partition, which carries {frozen_populations}",
        )

    # -- replicate unit ----------------------------------------------------------------
    contributing = tuple(sorted(
        sid for sid, level in values.items() if level in {spec.level_a, spec.level_b}
    ))
    donors = {sid: rec.donor_id for sid, rec in dataset.samples.items()}
    has_donor = all(donors.get(sid) for sid in contributing)
    # The replicate unit is the donor when every contributing sample declares one, and
    # the sample itself otherwise.  Mixing the two would make a resampled block
    # sometimes a donor and sometimes a sample.
    block_of = {sid: (str(donors[sid]) if has_donor else sid) for sid in contributing}
    block_unit = "donor_id" if has_donor else "sample_id"
    level_of = {sid: str(values[sid]) for sid in contributing}

    levels_in_block: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for sid in contributing:
        levels_in_block.setdefault(block_of[sid], set()).add(level_of[sid])
    complete = sorted(
        block for block, levels in levels_in_block.items()
        if levels == {spec.level_a, spec.level_b}
    )
    paired = has_donor and len(complete) >= MIN_PAIRED_DONORS
    if spec.model == "paired" and not paired:
        return ContrastRefusal(
            spec, "pairing_unsupported",
            f"the contrast declares a paired model but only {len(complete)} donor(s) "
            f"contribute both {spec.level_a!r} and {spec.level_b!r}; at least "
            f"{MIN_PAIRED_DONORS} complete donor pairs are required, and a donor factor is "
            + ("declared for every contributing sample" if has_donor
               else "not declared for every contributing sample"),
        )
    model = "paired" if paired else "unpaired"
    rows = tuple(complete) if paired else tuple(sorted(levels_in_block))
    index = {row: i for i, row in enumerate(rows)}

    if paired:
        # Each block is one donor holding both levels, so relabelling inside it is a swap
        # of that donor's two values, and every donor has exactly two such assignments.
        blocks = tuple((f"donor:{row}", (index[row],)) for row in rows)
        reachable = 2 ** len(rows)
    else:
        # Each block is a batch, and relabelling inside it permutes the labels among that
        # batch's own samples, so the number of each level in the batch cannot change.
        grouped: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
        for sid in contributing:
            grouped.setdefault(str(batch_values.get(sid)), []).append(index[block_of[sid]])
        blocks = tuple((f"batch:{b}", tuple(sorted(v))) for b, v in sorted(grouped.items()))
        holds_a = {
            row: any(level_of[s] == spec.level_a for s in contributing if block_of[s] == row)
            for row in rows
        }
        reachable = 1
        for _, indices in blocks:
            reachable *= math.comb(len(indices), sum(1 for i in indices if holds_a[rows[i]]))
            reachable = min(reachable, 10**9)

    return ContrastPlan(
        spec=spec,
        level_a=spec.level_a,
        level_b=spec.level_b,
        model=model,
        block_unit=block_unit,
        rows=rows,
        blocks=blocks,
        reachable_permutations=min(reachable, 10**9),
        contributing=contributing,
        block_of=block_of,
        level_of=level_of,
        markers=markers,
        populations=populations,
    )

docs.title: attach_emd_uncertainty(records, dataset, sampling, candidate_matrix, *, seed, n_resamples=BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES)
docs.text:
Attach donor-block bootstrap CIs to emd_within_population records, in place.

A record whose comparison has at least two donors per batch gains uncertainty_low/uncertainty_high and uncertainty_kind = 'donor_block_bootstrap_ci'. A record whose comparison does not keeps its value but states in the reason that no interval could be computed and why. Uncertainty is never silently omitted and never replaced by a zero-width interval.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/uncertainty.py 
def attach_emd_uncertainty(
    records: list[MetricRecord],
    dataset: Dataset,
    sampling: SamplingManifest,
    candidate_matrix: np.ndarray,
    *,
    seed: int,
    n_resamples: int = BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES,
) -> None:
    """Attach donor-block bootstrap CIs to ``emd_within_population`` records, in place.

    A record whose comparison has at least two donors per batch gains
    ``uncertainty_low``/``uncertainty_high`` and ``uncertainty_kind =
    'donor_block_bootstrap_ci'``.  A record whose comparison does not keeps its value
    but states in the reason that no interval could be computed and why.  Uncertainty
    is never silently omitted and never replaced by a zero-width interval.
    """
    obs = dataset.obs
    keep = obs[CELL_ID].isin(sampling.labels_by_cell.keys())
    obs = obs.loc[keep].copy()
    obs["_label"] = obs[CELL_ID].map(sampling.labels_by_cell)
    batch_of = dataset.sample_batches()
    obs["_batch"] = obs[SAMPLE_ID].map(batch_of).astype(str)
    positions = {cid: i for i, cid in enumerate(dataset.obs[CELL_ID])}
    obs["_row"] = obs[CELL_ID].map(positions)
    donor_of = {sid: rec.donor_id for sid, rec in dataset.samples.items()}
    obs["_donor"] = obs[SAMPLE_ID].map(donor_of).astype(str)

    markers = sampling.evaluation_markers
    if not markers:
        return
    feature_idx = dataset.feature_index(markers)
    col_of = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(markers)}

    for record in records:
        if record.metric_name != "emd_within_population":
            continue
        if record.status is not MetricStatus.OK:
            continue
        if record.population is None or record.marker is None:
            continue
        if record.comparison_id is None or "__vs__" not in record.comparison_id:
            continue
        batch_a, batch_b = record.comparison_id.split("__vs__", 1)
        rows = obs.loc[obs["_label"] == record.population]
        ra = rows.loc[rows["_batch"] == batch_a]
        rb = rows.loc[rows["_batch"] == batch_b]
        n_donors_a = ra["_donor"].nunique()
        n_donors_b = rb["_donor"].nunique()
        if n_donors_a < MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP or n_donors_b < MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP:
            record.reason = (
                (record.reason + "; " if record.reason else "")
                + f"no donor-block bootstrap CI: this comparison has {n_donors_a} "
                f"donor(s) in {batch_a} and {n_donors_b} in {batch_b}, and at least "
                f"{MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP} donors per batch are required to resample"
            )
            continue
        col = feature_idx[col_of[record.marker]]
        ci = donor_block_bootstrap_emd(
            candidate_matrix[ra["_row"].to_numpy(), col],
            candidate_matrix[rb["_row"].to_numpy(), col],
            ra["_donor"].to_numpy(),
            rb["_donor"].to_numpy(),
            n_resamples=n_resamples, seed=seed,
        )
        if ci is None:  # pragma: no cover - guarded by the donor count above
            continue
        record.uncertainty_low = ci[0]
        record.uncertainty_high = ci[1]
        record.uncertainty_kind = BOOTSTRAP_KIND
        record.reason = (
            (record.reason + "; " if record.reason else "")
            + f"donor-block bootstrap CI [{ci[0]:.4g}, {ci[1]:.4g}] "
            f"({BOOTSTRAP_ORIGIN})"
        )

docs.title: donor_block_bootstrap_emd(x, y, donors_x, donors_y, *, n_resamples=BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES, seed, level=0.95)
docs.text:
Percentile CI for the two-sample EMD, resampling donors within each group.

x and y are the two batches' cell values on one marker; donors_x and donors_y give each cell's donor. Donors are resampled with replacement within their own batch, never across batches. Returns None when either group has fewer than :data:MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP donors.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/uncertainty.py 
def donor_block_bootstrap_emd(
    x: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    donors_x: np.ndarray,
    donors_y: np.ndarray,
    *,
    n_resamples: int = BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES,
    seed: int,
    level: float = 0.95,
) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """Percentile CI for the two-sample EMD, resampling donors within each group.

    ``x`` and ``y`` are the two batches' cell values on one marker; ``donors_x`` and
    ``donors_y`` give each cell's donor.  Donors are resampled with replacement within
    their own batch, never across batches.  Returns ``None`` when either group has
    fewer than :data:`MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP` donors.
    """
    ux = np.unique(donors_x)
    uy = np.unique(donors_y)
    if len(ux) < MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP or len(uy) < MIN_DONORS_PER_GROUP:
        return None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    idx_x = {d: np.flatnonzero(donors_x == d) for d in ux}
    idx_y = {d: np.flatnonzero(donors_y == d) for d in uy}
    drawn = np.empty(n_resamples, dtype=float)
    for b in range(n_resamples):
        pick_x = rng.choice(len(ux), size=len(ux), replace=True)
        pick_y = rng.choice(len(uy), size=len(uy), replace=True)
        cells_x = np.concatenate([idx_x[ux[i]] for i in pick_x])
        cells_y = np.concatenate([idx_y[uy[i]] for i in pick_y])
        drawn[b] = stats.wasserstein_distance(x[cells_x], y[cells_y])
    alpha = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
    lo, hi = np.quantile(drawn, [alpha, 1.0 - alpha])
    return float(lo), float(hi)

docs.title: restricted_permutation_test(values, batch_labels, strata, *, n_permutations=PERMUTATION_RESAMPLES, seed)
docs.text:
Two-sided permutation test for a batch difference in means, within strata.

Batch labels are permuted only inside a stratum (a donor block at fixed protected-factor levels). A stratum contributes exchanges only when it contains both batch labels; every other stratum is held fixed. The test therefore never swaps labels across donor blocks and never across different protected levels — when no stratum holds both labels there is no valid exchange, and the p-value is reported as unavailable rather than as 1.0.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/metrics/uncertainty.py 
def restricted_permutation_test(
    values: np.ndarray,
    batch_labels: np.ndarray,
    strata: np.ndarray,
    *,
    n_permutations: int = PERMUTATION_RESAMPLES,
    seed: int,
) -> PermutationResult:
    """Two-sided permutation test for a batch difference in means, within strata.

    Batch labels are permuted only inside a stratum (a donor block at fixed
    protected-factor levels).  A stratum contributes exchanges only when it contains
    both batch labels; every other stratum is held fixed.  The test therefore never
    swaps labels across donor blocks and never across different protected levels —
    when no stratum holds both labels there is no valid exchange, and the p-value is
    reported as unavailable rather than as 1.0.
    """
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    labels = np.asarray(batch_labels, dtype=object)
    strata = np.asarray(strata, dtype=object)
    levels = sorted(set(labels.tolist()))
    if len(levels) != 2:
        return PermutationResult(
            observed=float("nan"), p_value=None, n_permutations=0,
            n_exchangeable_strata=0,
            reason=f"permutation test needs exactly two batch levels, got {levels}",
        )
    a, b = levels
    mask_a = labels == a
    if not mask_a.any() or not (~mask_a).any():
        return PermutationResult(
            observed=float("nan"), p_value=None, n_permutations=0,
            n_exchangeable_strata=0,
            reason="one batch level has no values; nothing is exchangeable",
        )
    observed = float(values[mask_a].mean() - values[~mask_a].mean())

    idx_by_key = {k: np.flatnonzero(strata == k) for k in np.unique(strata)}
    exchangeable = [
        idx for idx in idx_by_key.values()
        if set(labels[idx].tolist()) == {a, b}
    ]
    if not exchangeable:
        return PermutationResult(
            observed=observed, p_value=None, n_permutations=0, n_exchangeable_strata=0,
            reason=(
                "no stratum contains both batch labels, so no exchange is possible "
                "within donor blocks at fixed protected-factor levels; a permutation "
                "test would either do nothing or permute across different protected "
                "levels, and neither is valid"
            ),
        )

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    extreme = 0
    for _ in range(n_permutations):
        perm = labels.copy()
        for idx in exchangeable:
            perm[idx] = rng.permutation(labels[idx])
        stat = values[perm == a].mean() - values[perm != a].mean()
        if abs(stat) >= abs(observed):
            extreme += 1
    p_value = (1.0 + extreme) / (1.0 + n_permutations)
    return PermutationResult(
        observed=observed, p_value=float(p_value), n_permutations=n_permutations,
        n_exchangeable_strata=len(exchangeable),
    )

def stage_validate(config_path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path, layout: RunLayout) -> Path:
    """Validate the configuration and the input, then freeze the dataset manifest."""

    config = load_config(config_path)
    dataset = load_dataset(config, base_dir)
    dataset.assert_baseline_unchanged()

    # A declared upstream lock is a real input: if it is named, it must exist and
    # name the pinned commits the adapters were verified against. An unread lock
    # would let a configuration claim a pin it cannot enforce.
    if config.upstream.lock:
        lock_path = Path(base_dir) / config.upstream.lock
        if not lock_path.exists():
            raise ConfigError(
                f"upstream.lock names {config.upstream.lock!r} but the file does not "
                f"exist under {base_dir}; run scripts/fetch_upstream.sh or remove the key"
            )
        try:
            import yaml

            lock_data = yaml.safe_load(lock_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"upstream.lock {config.upstream.lock!r} is not valid YAML: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        if not isinstance(lock_data, dict) or not lock_data:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"upstream.lock {config.upstream.lock!r} must be a non-empty mapping of "
                "tool name to pinned commit"
            )

    _write_json(layout.resolved_config, {
        "config": config.resolved_dict(),
        "analytical_fingerprint": config.analytical_fingerprint(),
        "environment": environment_report(),
    })
    export_json_schemas(layout.schemas_dir)
    # When preprocessing is enabled the dataset manifest is frozen by stage_preprocess
    # from the reloaded baseline, so the counts the design audit sees are the post-QC
    # ones.  Writing the raw-input manifest here as well would put two contradictory
    # manifests behind one path, and the last writer would win silently.
    if not config.preprocessing.enabled:
        dataset.manifest.write(layout.dataset_manifest)
    return layout.dataset_manifest

def stage_preprocess(config_path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path, layout: RunLayout) -> Path:
    """Apply the declared preprocessing chain to the raw input and freeze the baseline.

    The chain is the one the configuration declares -- preliminary 2-D gating
    (``preprocess/gating.py``), the per-panel asinh transform (``preprocess/transform.py``,
    with the cofactor for each panel taken from ``preprocessing.cofactor_by_panel``),
    and the PeacoQC pass (``preprocess/peacoqc.py``) when a settings file declares one --
    applied in that order, because a gate is evaluated on the events the previous step
    kept and PeacoQC is evaluated on the transformed values the run will analyse.

    Four artifacts are written under the run's ``baseline/`` directory: the preprocessed
    baseline itself (immutable, the input every later stage loads), the per-event
    removal log (``preprocess/removals.py``), the processing manifest *of the baseline*
    (declared scale, compensated/unmixed null with a note, transformation provenance),
    and a summary of what each step did.  The dataset manifest is then frozen from the
    reloaded baseline, so cell identity and the per-sample counts the design audit sees
    are the post-QC ones and not the raw ones.
    """

    import anndata as ad
    import pandas as pd

    from batchdx.cyto.io.fcs import read_fcs
    from batchdx.cyto.io.hashing import file_sha256
    from batchdx.cyto.io.manifests import (
        read_marker_table,
        read_processing_manifest,
        read_sample_table,
        write_removed_events,
    )
    from batchdx.cyto.preprocess.gating import apply_gates, gates_from_config
    from batchdx.cyto.preprocess.peacoqc import (
        PeacoQCError,
        run_peacoqc,
        settings_from_config,
    )
    from batchdx.cyto.preprocess.removals import STEP_GATE, STEP_QC, empty_removal_log
    from batchdx.cyto.preprocess.transform import asinh_transform, resolve_convention

    config = load_config(config_path)
    if not config.preprocessing.enabled:
        raise ConfigError(
            "stage_preprocess: preprocessing.enabled is false; the stage exists only for "
            "a configuration that declares an upstream preprocessing step"
        )
    if config.input.format != "fcs":
        raise ConfigError(
            f"preprocessing: the declared input format is {config.input.format!r}; the "
            "preprocessing stage applies the declared chain to raw events, so it "
            "requires FCS input"
        )
    base = Path(base_dir)
    samples = {r.sample_id: r for r in read_sample_table(base / config.input.samples)}
    markers = read_marker_table(base / config.input.markers)
    raw_processing = read_processing_manifest(base / config.input.processing_manifest)
    marker_channels = [m.channel for m in markers]
    if any(c is None for c in marker_channels):
        unnamed = [
            m.feature_id for m, c in zip(markers, marker_channels, strict=True) if c is None
        ]
        raise ConfigError(
            f"marker manifest: feature(s) {unnamed} declare no channel, which FCS input "
            "requires; a marker without a channel cannot be read from raw events"
        )

    gate_table = gates_from_config(config, base_dir)
    qc_settings = settings_from_config(config, base_dir)
    convention = (
        resolve_convention(config.preprocessing.transformation)
        if config.preprocessing.transformation not in (None, "none") else None
    )
    cofactors = config.preprocessing.cofactor_by_panel
    panels = sorted({m.panel_id for m in markers if m.panel_id})
    if convention is not None:
        unpanelled = [m.feature_id for m in markers if not m.panel_id]
        if unpanelled:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"marker manifest: feature(s) {unpanelled} declare no panel_id; under "
                "the declared transformation every marker needs a panel, because a "
                "marker outside every declared panel would silently keep its raw scale "
                "in a baseline whose manifest says it was transformed"
            )
        missing = [p for p in panels if p not in cofactors]
        if missing:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"preprocessing.cofactor_by_panel: no cofactor is declared for panel(s) "
                f"{missing}; there is no universal cofactor, so the transform is refused "
                "rather than applied with a guessed one"
            )

    raw_dir = base / config.input.path
    blocks: list[np.ndarray] = []
    obs_rows: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    removals: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    gate_records: list[dict] = []
    qc_records: list[dict] = []
    qc_warnings: list[str] = []
    n_input_total = 0

    for sid, rec in samples.items():
        if not rec.source_file:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"sample {sid!r}: source_file is required for FCS input and is never "
                "inferred from file names"
            )
        path = raw_dir / rec.source_file
        contents = read_fcs(path)
        events = contents.events
        n = contents.n_events
        n_input_total += n
        index = np.arange(n, dtype=np.int64)
        ids = np.repeat(str(sid), n)
        keep = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
        if gate_table is not None:
            result = apply_gates(
                gate_table, events, contents.channel_names,
                sample_ids=ids, original_event_index=index, step=STEP_GATE,
            )
            keep = result.keep
            if len(result.removed):
                removals.append(result.removed)
            gate_records.extend({
                "step": STEP_GATE, "detail": (
                    f"gate {o.gate.name} ({o.gate.kind} over "
                    f"{'/'.join(o.gate.channels)}): kept {o.kept} of {o.n_input} events "
                    f"({o.removed} removed)"
                ),
            } for o in result.outcomes)
        kept = events[keep]
        kept_index = index[keep]
        if convention is not None:
            transformed = np.array(kept, copy=True)
            for panel in panels:
                cols = [
                    contents.channel_names.index(str(markers[j].channel))
                    for j in range(len(markers)) if markers[j].panel_id == panel
                ]
                transformed[:, cols] = asinh_transform(
                    transformed[:, cols], float(cofactors[panel])
                )
            kept = transformed
        if qc_settings is not None:
            qc = run_peacoqc(
                kept, contents.channel_names, sample_ids=ids[keep],
                original_event_index=kept_index, settings=qc_settings,
                work_dir=layout.baseline_dir / "peacoqc" / str(sid),
                rscript=config.upstream.rscript,
            )
            if len(qc.removed):
                removals.append(qc.removed)
                removed_here = qc.removed["original_event_index"].to_numpy(np.int64)
                alive = ~np.isin(kept_index, removed_here)
                kept, kept_index = kept[alive], kept_index[alive]
            for o in qc.samples:
                if o.n_input <= 0:
                    continue
                kept_fraction = (o.n_input - o.n_removed) / o.n_input
                if kept_fraction < PEACOQC_MIN_KEPT_FRACTION:
                    raise PeacoQCError(
                        f"sample {o.sample_id}: the PeacoQC pass kept "
                        f"{o.n_input - o.n_removed} of {o.n_input} events "
                        f"({kept_fraction:.1%}), below the "
                        f"{PEACOQC_MIN_KEPT_FRACTION:.0%} floor; a near-total removal "
                        "usually means the QC channel's distribution defeated peak "
                        "detection rather than that the sample was that contaminated, "
                        "and a baseline built from the survivors would misrepresent "
                        "the sample"
                    )
            qc_records.extend({
                "step": STEP_QC, "detail": (
                    f"sample {o.sample_id}: kept {o.n_input - o.n_removed} of "
                    f"{o.n_input} events ({o.n_removed} removed); criteria applied: "
                    f"{', '.join(o.criteria_applied) or 'none'}"
                ),
            } for o in qc.samples)
            qc_warnings.extend(qc.warnings)

        cols = [contents.channel_names.index(str(c)) for c in marker_channels]
        blocks.append(kept[:, cols])
        checksum = file_sha256(path)
        obs_rows.append(pd.DataFrame({
            "sample_id": np.repeat(str(sid), kept.shape[0]),
            "original_event_index": kept_index,
            "acquisition_order": kept_index,
            "source_checksum": np.repeat(checksum, kept.shape[0]),
        }))

    matrix = np.vstack(blocks) if blocks else np.zeros((0, len(marker_channels)))
    obs = pd.concat(obs_rows, ignore_index=True)
    adata = ad.AnnData(
        X=np.zeros((matrix.shape[0], matrix.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32),
        obs=obs,
        var=pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index([m.feature_id for m in markers], dtype=object)),
    )
    adata.layers[BASELINE_LAYER] = matrix
    layout.preprocess_baseline.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    adata.write_h5ad(layout.preprocess_baseline)

    log = pd.concat(removals, ignore_index=True) if removals else empty_removal_log()
    write_removed_events(log, layout.removal_log)
    by_step = log.groupby("step").size().to_dict() if len(log) else {}

    scale = (
        "asinh (per-panel cofactors: "
        + ", ".join(f"{p}={float(cofactors[p]):g}" for p in panels) + ")"
        if convention is not None else str(raw_processing.scale)
    )
    processing = {
        "compensated": None,
        "unmixed": None,
        "compensation_source": None,
        "qc_history": [r["detail"] for r in gate_records + qc_records],
        "transformation": convention.name if convention is not None else None,
        "transformation_parameters": (
            {f"cofactor[{p}]": float(cofactors[p]) for p in panels}
            if convention is not None else {}
        ),
        "scale": scale,
        "units": (
            "arcsinh units (per-panel cofactors)" if convention is not None
            else raw_processing.units
        ),
        "corrected": False,
        "notes": (
            "written by batchdx.cyto.pipeline.stage_preprocess from the raw input "
            f"({config.input.path}); compensated/unmixed are null because the raw "
            f"processing manifest ({config.input.processing_manifest}) declares "
            f"compensated={raw_processing.compensated}, unmixed={raw_processing.unmixed} "
            "and this stage performs neither, so it does not re-assert them"
        ),
    }
    layout.baseline_processing_manifest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    layout.baseline_processing_manifest.write_text(
        json.dumps(processing, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )

    _write_json(layout.preprocess_summary, {
        "n_events_input": n_input_total,
        "n_events_kept": int(matrix.shape[0]),
        "n_events_removed": n_input_total - int(matrix.shape[0]),
        "n_samples": len(samples),
        "steps": gate_records + qc_records,
        "removals_by_step": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in by_step.items()},
        "declared": {
            "gating": config.preprocessing.gating,
            "transformation": config.preprocessing.transformation,
            "cofactor_by_panel": {str(k): float(v) for k, v in cofactors.items()},
            "peacoqc": config.preprocessing.peacoqc,
        },
        "processing": processing,
        "warnings": qc_warnings,
    })

    # The manifest is frozen from the reloaded baseline, not from the in-memory frame,
    # so cell identity and the per-sample counts are exactly what every later stage
    # will load -- the same guarantee stage_validate gives the raw input.
    dataset = load_dataset(_baseline_config(config, layout), base_dir)
    dataset.manifest.write(layout.dataset_manifest)
    return layout.dataset_manifest

def stage_correct(
    candidate_id: str, config_path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path, layout: RunLayout
) -> Path:
    """Run one correction candidate from the immutable baseline."""

    config, dataset = _load(config_path, base_dir, layout)
    design = DesignAudit.read(layout.design_audit)
    sampling = (
        SamplingManifest.read(layout.sampling_manifest)
        if layout.sampling_manifest.exists() else None
    )
    spec = next((c for c in config.correction.candidates if c.id == candidate_id), None)
    if spec is None:
        raise KeyError(f"candidate {candidate_id!r} is not in the configuration")

    context = BackendContext(
        design=design, sampling=sampling,
        work_dir=str(layout.candidate_dir(candidate_id) / "work"),
        seed=config.project.seed, rscript=config.upstream.rscript,
        upstream_dir=config.upstream.checkout_dir,
    )
    backend = get_backend(spec.backend)

    # A retry invalidates its previous success before anything can fail or be cancelled.
    for path in (layout.correction_result(candidate_id), layout.corrected_h5ad(candidate_id),
                 layout.metric_result(candidate_id)):
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    log_path = layout.root / "logs" / f"correct_{candidate_id}.log"
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log_path.write_text(f"Starting candidate {candidate_id!r} ({spec.backend}).\n", encoding="utf-8")

    eligibility = next(
        (e for e in design.eligibility if e.name == spec.backend and e.kind == "backend"), None
    )
    waived: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    override_note: str | None = None
    if eligibility is not None and not eligibility.eligible:
        if config.design.allow_exploratory_override and eligibility.override_allowed:
            # The gate is bypassed, not satisfied, and the bypass is recorded before the
            # backend runs so that a crash downstream cannot erase the fact that it was
            # attempted.  Three places carry it: this audit file, which stage_decide
            # turns into ``DecisionResult.overrides`` for the report; the waiver on the
            # correction result, so a reader of that artifact alone still sees it; and
            # the warning below, in the same words for both.
            waived = [{
                "candidate_id": candidate_id,
                "backend": spec.backend,
                "reason_code": eligibility.reason_code or "unknown",
                "reason": eligibility.reason or "",
                "allowed_by": "design.allow_exploratory_override",
            }]
            override_note = _record_exploratory_override(layout, {
                "candidate_id": candidate_id,
                "backend": spec.backend,
                "overrode": f"{eligibility.reason} (reason code: {eligibility.reason_code})",
                "declared_by": "design.allow_exploratory_override = true",
                "effect": (
                    "the backend was run on a design its own eligibility rule rejects. "
                    "Its output is exploratory: it is scored and displayed, and it cannot "
                    "support a recommendation"
                ),
            })
        else:
            record = make_spec(candidate_id, spec.backend, None, dict(spec.parameters),
                               config.project.seed, dataset, [])
            return _write_failure_candidate(
                dataset, layout, candidate_id, record, CorrectionStatus.INELIGIBLE,
                f"{eligibility.reason} (reason code: {eligibility.reason_code})",
                context, backend,
            )

    # Only expected candidate execution/output errors are reportable candidate
    # failures; shared input loading above and cancellation remain whole-run failures.
    # OutputValidationError (a ValueError): the backend produced a non-finite or
    # reshaped matrix.  FileNotFoundError (an OSError): the R script never wrote its
    # output.  JSONDecodeError (a ValueError): the R script's result payload is
    # unparseable.  TimeoutExpired: the R script overran its budget.
    candidate_errors = (
        BackendError, OutputValidationError, ValueError, OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
    )

    def _record_for_exc(exc: Exception) -> CandidateSpecRecord:
        try:
            resolved = resolve_parameters(backend.capabilities, dict(spec.parameters))
        except BackendError:
            resolved = dict(spec.parameters)
        return make_spec(candidate_id, spec.backend, None, resolved,
                         config.project.seed, dataset, [])

    try:
        matrix, result = backend.run(dataset, candidate_id, dict(spec.parameters), context)
    except BackendNotAvailable as exc:
        # Availability is a property of the environment, decided by the exception
        # type, never by sniffing the error text.
        with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(traceback.format_exc())
        return _write_failure_candidate(
            dataset, layout, candidate_id, _record_for_exc(exc),
            CorrectionStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE, str(exc), context, backend,
            extra_warnings=[override_note] if override_note else None,
        )
    except BackendIneligible as exc:
        # A design-coverage refusal is a statement about the data, recorded as
        # INELIGIBLE rather than NOT_AVAILABLE: the package is installed, the split
        # simply cannot support the fit.  The branch precedes the generic
        # candidate_errors branch, which would otherwise file the same refusal as
        # FAILED because BackendIneligible is a BackendError.
        with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(traceback.format_exc())
        return _write_failure_candidate(
            dataset, layout, candidate_id, _record_for_exc(exc),
            CorrectionStatus.INELIGIBLE, str(exc), context, backend,
            extra_warnings=[override_note] if override_note else None,
        )
    except candidate_errors as exc:
        with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(traceback.format_exc())
        return _write_failure_candidate(
            dataset, layout, candidate_id, _record_for_exc(exc),
            CorrectionStatus.FAILED, str(exc), context, backend,
            extra_warnings=[override_note] if override_note else None,
        )

    if result.status is not CorrectionStatus.SUCCESS:
        # The backend reported its own failure and returned no matrix; record that
        # failure rather than exporting whatever came back.
        return _write_failure_candidate(
            dataset, layout, candidate_id, result.candidate,
            result.status, result.reason or "the backend reported failure",
            context, backend,
            extra_warnings=[override_note] if override_note else None,
        )

    try:
        path = write_candidate_output(
            dataset, matrix, layout.corrected_h5ad(candidate_id),
            candidate_id=candidate_id, output_scale=result.output_scale,
        )
    except candidate_errors as exc:
        # A partial export is removed: a file that is half an H5AD must never be
        # readable as a corrected output.  The failure candidate writes the
        # unmodified baseline in its place, so the declared output exists and the
        # result records that it is not a correction.
        with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(traceback.format_exc())
        layout.corrected_h5ad(candidate_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return _write_failure_candidate(
            dataset, layout, candidate_id, _record_for_exc(exc),
            CorrectionStatus.FAILED, str(exc), context, backend,
            extra_warnings=[override_note] if override_note else None,
        )

    result.output_path = str(path)
    result.waived_eligibility = waived
    if waived:
        result.warnings = list(result.warnings) + [
            f"EXPLORATORY OVERRIDE: {w['backend']} ran on a design its own eligibility "
            f"rule rejects ({w['reason'] or 'unknown'}; reason code: {w['reason_code']}), "
            "because design.allow_exploratory_override = true. Its output is exploratory "
            "and cannot support a recommendation."
            for w in waived
        ]
    result.write(layout.correction_result(candidate_id))
    with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        log.write(f"Status: {result.status.value}. {result.reason or 'completed'}\n")
    return layout.correction_result(candidate_id)

def stage_metrics(
    candidate_id: str, config_path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path, layout: RunLayout
) -> Path:
    """Score one candidate on the frozen common partition."""

    config, dataset = _load(config_path, base_dir, layout)
    design = DesignAudit.read(layout.design_audit)
    sampling = SamplingManifest.read(layout.sampling_manifest)
    correction = CorrectionResult.read(layout.correction_result(candidate_id))
    matrix = _read_candidate_matrix(dataset, layout, candidate_id, correction)

    if matrix is None:
        MetricResult(
            run_id=config.project.id, candidate_id=candidate_id, metric_group="common",
            status="ineligible",
            reason=(
                f"candidate {candidate_id!r} has status {correction.status.value}: "
                f"{correction.reason or 'no corrected output was produced'}. "
                "A missing metric is not a zero score."
            ),
        ).write(layout.metric_result(candidate_id))
        return layout.metric_result(candidate_id)

    result = compute_common_metrics(
        dataset, matrix, sampling, design,
        run_id=config.project.id, candidate_id=candidate_id,
    )


    # The native namespace is optional by construction: it calls upstream R and cannot
    # run without cyCombine.  A failure here is recorded as a status on those two specs
    # and never removes the common-namespace records, so an environment gap costs the
    # native numbers and nothing else.  Only the identity candidate is compared against
    # itself, because a native reduction is a ratio of the corrected and uncorrected
    # states and the identity is the only candidate whose uncorrected state is itself.
    if candidate_id == _identity_candidate_id(config):
        try:
            from batchdx.cyto.metrics.native import compute_native_metrics

            result.records.extend(compute_native_metrics(
                dataset, dataset.expression(), matrix, sampling, design,
                run_id=config.project.id, candidate_id=candidate_id,
                context=BackendContext(
                    design=design, sampling=sampling,
                    work_dir=str(layout.candidate_dir(candidate_id) / "native"),
                    seed=config.project.seed, rscript=config.upstream.rscript,
                    upstream_dir=config.upstream.checkout_dir,
                ),
                work_dir=str(layout.candidate_dir(candidate_id) / "native"),
            ))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a status is the point
            from batchdx.cyto.metrics.records import metric_record
            from batchdx.cyto.metrics.registry import NATIVE_CYCOMBINE_EMD

            # One record, carrying the same fields every other metric record carries, so
            # the failure is visible in the same place a value would have been and cannot
            # be mistaken for an omitted metric.
            result.records.append(metric_record(
                NATIVE_CYCOMBINE_EMD, sampling,
                run_id=config.project.id,
                candidate_id=candidate_id,
                status=MetricStatus.FAILED,
                reason=f"the native-namespace metrics could not be produced: {exc}",
                n_samples=0, n_cells=0, coverage=0.0, aggregation_weight=1.0,
            ))


    if config.design.biological_contrasts:
        result.records.extend(compute_biological_contrasts(
            dataset, dataset.expression(), matrix, sampling, design,
            config.design.biological_contrasts,
            run_id=config.project.id, candidate_id=candidate_id,
            donor_factor=config.design.donor,
        ))

    result.write(layout.metric_result(candidate_id))
    return layout.metric_result(candidate_id)

def stage_decide(
    config_path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path, layout: RunLayout
) -> Path:
    """Aggregate, compute reductions, and assign a state to every candidate."""

    config = load_config(config_path)
    design = DesignAudit.read(layout.design_audit)
    sampling = SamplingManifest.read(layout.sampling_manifest)

    # The sample table is re-read here only to answer the held-out question, which is a
    # question about which samples sit in which split.  It is not part of the frozen
    # manifest, and passing it keeps the decision layer free of any dataset handle.
    _, dataset = _load(config_path, base_dir, layout)

    corrections: dict[str, CorrectionResult] = {}
    metrics: dict[str, MetricResult] = {}
    for candidate in config.correction.candidates:
        path = layout.correction_result(candidate.id)
        if path.exists():
            corrections[candidate.id] = CorrectionResult.read(path)
        mpath = layout.metric_result(candidate.id)
        if mpath.exists():
            metrics[candidate.id] = MetricResult.read(mpath)

    identity = _identity_candidate_id(config)
    reductions = compute_reductions(
        metrics, sampling, run_id=config.project.id, identity_candidate_id=identity
    )
    _write_json(layout.reductions, {"records": [r.model_dump(mode="json") for r in reductions]})

    # Surface any waived eligibility constraints on the decision record, so the
    # override audit trail promised by the assessment layer exists in real runs. Read
    # from the audit file rather than rebuilt from the correction results: the file is
    # written before the backend runs, so a candidate that crashed mid-correction is
    # still accounted for here.
    overrides = _read_exploratory_overrides(layout)

    decision = assess_candidates(
        design, sampling, corrections, metrics, reductions,
        samples=dict(dataset.samples),
        run_id=config.project.id, policy_name=config.evaluation.policy,
        identity_candidate_id=identity, overrides=overrides,
    )
    decision.write(layout.decision)
    return layout.decision

def stage_status(config_path: str | Path, layout: RunLayout) -> Path:
    """Summarise what ran, what was skipped, and why.  Never inferred from directories."""

    config = load_config(config_path)
    entries: list[StageStatus] = []

    for name, flag in DETECTOR_FLAGS.items():
        requested = getattr(config.detectors, flag)
        path = layout.detector_result(name)
        if not requested:
            entries.append(StageStatus(stage="diagnose", unit=name, status="skipped",
                                       reason="not requested in the configuration"))
        elif not path.exists():
            entries.append(StageStatus(stage="diagnose", unit=name, status="failed",
                                       reason="the detector produced no result file"))
        else:
            from batchdx.cyto.schemas.contracts import DetectorResult

            result = DetectorResult.read(path)
            mapped = {"ok": "ok", "ineligible": "ineligible", "failed": "failed",
                      "not_available": "blocked"}[result.status]
            entries.append(StageStatus(stage="diagnose", unit=name, status=mapped,
                                       reason=result.reason or "completed"))

    for candidate in config.correction.candidates:
        path = layout.correction_result(candidate.id)
        if not path.exists():
            entries.append(StageStatus(stage="correct", unit=candidate.id, status="failed",
                                       reason="no correction result file was written"))
            continue
        result = CorrectionResult.read(path)
        mapped = {
            CorrectionStatus.SUCCESS: "ok",
            CorrectionStatus.INELIGIBLE: "ineligible",
            CorrectionStatus.FAILED: "failed",
            CorrectionStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE: "blocked",
        }[result.status]
        entries.append(StageStatus(stage="correct", unit=candidate.id, status=mapped,
                                   reason=result.reason or "completed"))

    _write_json(layout.status, {
        "run_id": config.project.id,
        "analytical_fingerprint": config.analytical_fingerprint(),
        "environment": environment_report(),
        "entries": [e.model_dump(mode="json") for e in entries],
    })
    return layout.status

docs.title: batchdx.cyto.preprocess
docs.text:
Upstream preprocessing: gating, the fluorescence transform, and PeacoQC.

This package is deliberately outside the run the pipeline performs. The correction workflow reads an already-preprocessed baseline and never transforms events; that contract is stated in PreprocessingConfig and in _validate_processing (io/dataset.py:143-152), and nothing here changes it.

What this package is for is the step before the baseline exists: taking raw FCS, removing debris, singlets and dead cells on the geometry the reference implementation uses, applying the arcsinh the reference implementation applies, running PeacoQC, and — the part that did not exist before — recording which events each of those steps removed and why, in the four columns Dataset.removed_events has always declared.

Three modules, each refusing rather than approximating:

  • :mod:~batchdx.cyto.preprocess.gating — two-dimensional rectangle and polygon gates. Not sampling.partitions.GatingRule, which is one-dimensional and labels cells instead of removing them; the module docstring says why one-dimensional gating would be a strictly weaker gate under the same name.
  • :mod:~batchdx.cyto.preprocess.transform — asinh(raw / cofactor), the convention :mod:batchdx.cyto.io.export inverts exactly, with the cross-check against the exporter executed rather than asserted in prose.
  • :mod:~batchdx.cyto.preprocess.peacoqc — PeacoQC::PeacoQC from the installed Bioconductor package, keeping the !GoodCells index the reference implementation discards, and reporting an isolation tree that declined to run as a status.

One gate: a name, a kind, and the coordinates it is drawn with.

bounds is a tuple of (low, high) intervals, one per axis, for a rectangle. vertices is an (n, 2) array of polygon vertices in (mk1, mk2) order for a polygon. Exactly one of the two is populated, and which one is decided by kind rather than by which happens to be non-empty.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Gate:
    """One gate: a name, a kind, and the coordinates it is drawn with.

    ``bounds`` is a tuple of ``(low, high)`` intervals, one per axis, for a
    ``rectangle``.  ``vertices`` is an ``(n, 2)`` array of polygon vertices in
    ``(mk1, mk2)`` order for a ``polygon``.  Exactly one of the two is populated, and
    which one is decided by ``kind`` rather than by which happens to be non-empty.
    """

    name: str
    kind: Literal["rectangle", "polygon"]
    mk1: str
    mk2: str | None = None
    bounds: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...] = ()
    vertices: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None, repr=False)

    @property
    def channels(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return (self.mk1,) if self.mk2 is None else (self.mk1, self.mk2)

    @property
    def reason(self) -> str:
        """The criterion this gate names, as it appears in a removal log."""

        axes = "/".join(self.channels)
        if self.kind == "rectangle":
            spans = ",".join(f"[{lo:g},{hi:g}]" for lo, hi in self.bounds)
            return f"{self.name}:rectangle({axes}={spans})"
        assert self.vertices is not None
        return f"{self.name}:polygon({axes},{len(self.vertices)} vertices)"

    def contains(self, x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
        """Boolean mask of the events this gate **keeps**.

        The name is deliberate: a gate's job is to keep what is inside it, and the
        reference implementation's ``Subset`` removes everything else.  Nothing here
        ever returns the complement silently.
        """

        if self.kind == "rectangle":
            if y is None:
                low, high = self.bounds[0]
                return (x >= low) & (x <= high)
            keep = np.ones(x.shape, dtype=bool)
            for axis, (low, high) in zip((x, y), self.bounds, strict=True):
                keep &= (axis >= low) & (axis <= high)
            return keep
        if y is None:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {self.name!r} is a polygon, which needs two channels; it declares "
                f"only {self.mk1!r}. A one-dimensional gate is declared as "
                "'type: rectangle'"
            )
        assert self.vertices is not None
        return points_in_polygon(x, y, self.vertices)

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """Refuse a gate this build cannot evaluate, before it is applied to anything."""

        if self.kind not in GATE_KINDS:  # pragma: no cover - read_gates checks first
            raise GatingError(f"gate {self.name!r}: unknown kind {self.kind!r}")
        if self.kind == "rectangle":
            if not self.bounds:
                raise GatingError(
                    f"gate {self.name!r}: a rectangle needs one (low, high) interval per "
                    "channel"
                )
            if self.mk2 is None and len(self.bounds) != 1:
                raise GatingError(
                    f"gate {self.name!r}: declares one channel {self.mk1!r} but "
                    f"{len(self.bounds)} intervals"
                )
            if self.mk2 is not None and len(self.bounds) != 2:
                raise GatingError(
                    f"gate {self.name!r}: declares two channels "
                    f"({self.mk1}, {self.mk2}) but {len(self.bounds)} intervals"
                )
            for low, high in self.bounds:
                if not (np.isfinite(low) and np.isfinite(high)) or high < low:
                    raise GatingError(
                        f"gate {self.name!r}: interval [{low}, {high}] is not a finite, "
                        "ordered range"
                    )
            return
        if self.vertices is None or self.vertices.ndim != 2 or self.vertices.shape[1] != 2:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {self.name!r}: a polygon needs an (n, 2) list of (mk1, mk2) vertices"
            )
        if self.vertices.shape[0] < 3:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {self.name!r}: a polygon needs at least three vertices, got "
                f"{self.vertices.shape[0]}"
            )
        if not np.isfinite(self.vertices).all():
            raise GatingError(f"gate {self.name!r}: polygon vertices must be finite")
        if self.mk2 is None:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {self.name!r}: a polygon needs two channels; it declares only "
                f"{self.mk1!r}"
            )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GateTable:
    """An ordered chain of gates, plus the channels they need."""

    gates: tuple[Gate, ...]
    channels: tuple[str, ...]

    def validate(self, available: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = ()) -> None:
        for gate in self.gates:
            gate.validate()
        missing = [c for c in self.channels if c not in set(available)]
        if missing:
            raise GatingError(
                f"the gate table needs channel(s) {missing}, which the data does not carry. "
                "Gate channels are scatter and viability parameters, not panel markers: "
                "declare them in the marker manifest or supply an FCS that has them. A "
                "missing channel is not zero, and a gate on a constant zero would remove "
                "either everything or nothing"
            )

    def to_frame(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            [
                {
                    "name": g.name,
                    "kind": g.kind,
                    "mk1": g.mk1,
                    "mk2": g.mk2 or "",
                    "channels": "/".join(g.channels),
                    "reason": g.reason,
                }
                for g in self.gates
            ]
        )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PeacoQCResult:
    """The removal log, the per-sample outcomes, and the software that produced them.

    ``output_files`` is what PeacoQC actually wrote, counted and named by the script
    rather than predicted.  ``report = TRUE`` is not a promise PeacoQC keeps on every
    route -- it writes no report when ``determine_good_cells = "MAD"`` -- so the
    artifact is reported as it is, and a settings file asking for a report on a route
    that produces none is visible instead of silently unfulfilled.
    """

    removed: pd.DataFrame
    samples: tuple[SampleQCOutcome, ...]
    software: tuple[SoftwareVersion, ...] = ()
    warnings: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    status: str = "ok"
    reason: str | None = None
    report_paths: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    output_files: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def n_removed(self) -> int:
        return int(len(self.removed))

    def per_sample(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        rows = [
            {
                "sample_id": s.sample_id,
                "n_input": s.n_input,
                "n_removed": s.n_removed,
                "removed_fraction": s.removed_fraction,
                "it_fraction": s.it_fraction,
                "mad_fraction": s.mad_fraction,
                "criteria_applied": "/".join(s.criteria_applied),
                "it_available": s.it_available,
                "it_reason": s.it_reason or "",
            }
            for s in self.samples
        ]
        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    peak_removal: float = 1.0 / 3.0
    min_nr_bins_peakdetection: int = 10
    time_channel: str | None = None
    plot: bool | str | int | float = False
    report: bool = True

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # YAML and JSON both hand back a list for a sequence and a bare string for a
        # scalar, so ``channels: CD4`` and ``channels: [CD4]`` are the same declaration.
        # Coerced here rather than at the call site, because a reader that returned a
        # one-element list would compare unequal to a one-element tuple everywhere
        # downstream and the difference is a spelling, not a setting.
        if isinstance(self.channels, str):
            coerced: tuple[str, ...] = (self.channels,)
        else:
            coerced = tuple(str(c) for c in self.channels)
        object.__setattr__(self, "channels", coerced)
        if not self.channels:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                "PeacoQC needs at least one channel to evaluate; a QC call over an empty "
                "channel list would remove nothing and report success"
            )
        if self.criteria not in CRITERIA:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                f"determine_good_cells={self.criteria!r} is not one of {list(CRITERIA)}; "
                "the reference implementation refuses anything else (QC.R:144)"
            )
        if self.mad <= 0 or self.it_limit <= 0:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                f"MAD={self.mad} and IT_limit={self.it_limit} must both be positive; a "
                "non-positive threshold would flag every measurement or none, and neither "
                "is a quality criterion"
            )
        if self.step <= 0 or self.min_cells <= 0 or self.max_bins <= 0:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                "min_cells, max_bins and step are counts and must be positive; "
                f"got min_cells={self.min_cells}, max_bins={self.max_bins}, step={self.step}"
            )
        if self.criteria in {"all", "MAD"} and self.mad is None:  # pragma: no cover
            raise PeacoQCError("criteria requires a MAD value")

    @property
    def reason(self) -> str:
        """The criterion named in the removal log, naming only what was actually asked."""

        parts = [f"determine_good_cells={self.criteria}"]
        if self.criteria in {"all", "MAD"}:
            parts.append(f"MAD={self.mad:g}")
        if self.criteria in {"all", "IT"}:
            parts.append(f"IT_limit={self.it_limit:g}")
        return f"PeacoQC{VERIFIED_VERSION}:" + ",".join(parts)

    def to_params(self, output_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "channels": list(self.channels),
            "criteria": self.criteria,
            "mad": float(self.mad),
            "it_limit": float(self.it_limit),
            "min_cells": int(self.min_cells),
            "max_bins": int(self.max_bins),
            "step": int(self.step),
            "consecutive_bins": int(self.consecutive_bins),
            "remove_zeros": bool(self.remove_zeros),
            "force_IT": int(self.force_IT),
            "peak_removal": float(self.peak_removal),
            "min_nr_bins_peakdetection": int(self.min_nr_bins_peakdetection),
            "time_channel_parameter": self.time_channel,
            "plot": self.plot,
            "report": bool(self.report),
            "output_dir": str(output_dir),
        }

docs.title: apply_gates(table, values, channels, *, sample_ids, original_event_index, step='prelim_gating')
docs.text:
Apply every gate in order and return what survived plus why the rest did not.

values is (n_events, n_channels) over channels. The gates are applied to the events still alive at each step, exactly as a sequence of Subset calls would, so a point outside the debris gate is not also counted as failing the singlets gate: it is counted once, at the gate that removed it.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/gating.py 
def apply_gates(
    table: GateTable,
    values: np.ndarray,
    channels: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    sample_ids: np.ndarray,
    original_event_index: np.ndarray,
    step: str = "prelim_gating",
) -> GatingResult:
    """Apply every gate in order and return what survived plus why the rest did not.

    ``values`` is ``(n_events, n_channels)`` over ``channels``.  The gates are applied
    to the events still alive at each step, exactly as a sequence of ``Subset`` calls
    would, so a point outside the debris gate is not also counted as failing the singlets
    gate: it is counted once, at the gate that removed it.
    """

    table.validate(channels)
    index_of = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(channels)}
    missing_values = [c for c in table.channels if c not in index_of]
    if missing_values:  # pragma: no cover - validate() already refuses this
        raise GatingError(f"the data does not carry gate channel(s) {missing_values}")

    n = int(values.shape[0])
    alive = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
    outcomes: list[GateOutcome] = []
    rows: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for gate in table.gates:
        x = values[:, index_of[gate.mk1]]
        y = None if gate.mk2 is None else values[:, index_of[gate.mk2]]
        keep = gate.contains(x, y) & alive
        removed_mask = alive & ~keep
        n_removed = int(removed_mask.sum())
        if n_removed:
            rows.append(
                pd.DataFrame(
                    {
                        "sample_id": np.asarray(sample_ids)[removed_mask],
                        "original_event_index": np.asarray(original_event_index)[removed_mask],
                        "step": step,
                        "reason": gate.reason,
                    }
                )
            )
        per_sample = {
            str(sid): int(c)
            for sid, c in zip(
                *np.unique(np.asarray(sample_ids)[removed_mask], return_counts=True),
                strict=True,
            )
        }
        outcomes.append(
            GateOutcome(
                gate=gate,
                kept=int(keep.sum()),
                removed=n_removed,
                n_input=int(alive.sum()),
                removed_by_sample=per_sample,
            )
        )
        alive = keep

    removed = (
        pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
        if rows
        else pd.DataFrame(columns=["sample_id", "original_event_index", "step", "reason"])
    )
    return GatingResult(keep=alive, outcomes=tuple(outcomes), removed=removed)

def gates_from_config(config, base_dir: str | Path = ".") -> GateTable | None:
    """The gate table ``preprocessing.gating`` declares, or ``None`` if it declares none.

    This is the reader that makes ``preprocessing.gating`` a key rather than a promise.
    It reads the key and nothing else: the gate channels come from the table, the order
    comes from the chain, and no channel is inferred from the panel.

    if declared is None:
        return None
    return read_gates(Path(base_dir) / str(declared))

docs.title: points_in_polygon(x, y, vertices)
docs.text:
Even-odd (crossing-number) test, vectorised over events.

Written out rather than delegated to a plotting package so that a gate has no dependency this package would have to declare, and so the boundary convention is visible: a point exactly on an edge may be counted either way by this rule, which is the same freedom flowCore::polygonGate does not take. For cytometry scatter data, where coordinates are continuous, the boundary set has measure zero; the fact is recorded rather than pretended away.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/gating.py 
def points_in_polygon(
    x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, vertices: np.ndarray
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Even-odd (crossing-number) test, vectorised over events.

    Written out rather than delegated to a plotting package so that a gate has no
    dependency this package would have to declare, and so the boundary convention is
    visible: a point exactly on an edge may be counted either way by this rule, which is
    the same freedom ``flowCore::polygonGate`` does not take.  For cytometry scatter
    data, where coordinates are continuous, the boundary set has measure zero; the fact
    is recorded rather than pretended away.
    """

    v = np.asarray(vertices, dtype=np.float64)
    px = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    py = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    inside = np.zeros(px.shape, dtype=bool)
    n = v.shape[0]
    j = n - 1
    for i in range(n):
        xi, yi = v[i]
        xj, yj = v[j]
        straddles = (yi > py) != (yj > py)
        if not straddles.any():
            j = i
            continue
        # x coordinate of the edge at this point's y, only where the edge straddles it
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            crossing = (xj - xi) * (py - yi) / (yj - yi) + xi
        inside ^= straddles & (px < crossing)
        j = i
    return inside

docs.title: read_gates(path)
docs.text:
Read a gate table in the reference implementation's own YAML shape.

The shape is gate_chain (the order to apply) plus gates keyed by name, each entry carrying filterId, mk1, optional mk2, type and coords. It is read rather than reinterpreted, so a table written for prelim_gating.R loads here unchanged and a divergence shows up as a parse error.

The order is the chain's, and it matters: the reference implementation applies its gates in sequence to the surviving events, so a point outside the first gate is never offered to the second. The order is preserved here for the same reason.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/gating.py 
def read_gates(path: str | Path) -> GateTable:
    """Read a gate table in the reference implementation's own YAML shape.

    The shape is ``gate_chain`` (the order to apply) plus ``gates`` keyed by name, each
    entry carrying ``filterId``, ``mk1``, optional ``mk2``, ``type`` and ``coords``.  It
    is read rather than reinterpreted, so a table written for ``prelim_gating.R`` loads
    here unchanged and a divergence shows up as a parse error.

    The order is the chain's, and it matters: the reference implementation applies its
    gates in sequence to the surviving events, so a point outside the first gate is
    never offered to the second.  The order is preserved here for the same reason.
    """

    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        raise GatingError(f"gate table not found: {p}")
    try:
        raw = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
        raise GatingError(f"{p}: not valid YAML: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise GatingError(f"{p}: top level of a gate table must be a mapping")
    declared = raw.get("gates")
    if not isinstance(declared, dict) or not declared:
        raise GatingError(f"{p}: 'gates' must be a non-empty mapping of gate name to geometry")
    chain = raw.get("gate_chain")
    if chain is None:
        names = list(declared)
    else:
        names = [str(n) for n in chain]
        unknown = [n for n in names if n not in declared]
        if unknown:
            raise GatingError(
                f"{p}: gate_chain names gate(s) {unknown} that 'gates' does not define"
            )
        unused = [n for n in declared if n not in set(names)]
        if unused:
            raise GatingError(
                f"{p}: gate(s) {unused} are defined but not in gate_chain. A gate that is "
                "declared and never applied is the accepted-and-ignored outcome this "
                "package refuses; list it in the chain or delete it"
            )

    gates: list[Gate] = []
    for name in names:
        spec = declared[name] or {}
        kind = str(spec.get("type", "")).strip().lower()
        if kind in UNIMPLEMENTED_GATE_KINDS:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {name!r}: type {kind!r} is not implemented by this build, because "
                f"{UNIMPLEMENTED_GATE_KINDS[kind]}. Declaring it and then not applying it "
                "would report a gate that was never evaluated as a gate that passed"
            )
        if kind not in GATE_KINDS:
            raise GatingError(
                f"gate {name!r}: type {kind!r} is not one of {list(GATE_KINDS)}"
            )
        mk1 = spec.get("mk1")
        if not mk1:
            raise GatingError(f"gate {name!r}: 'mk1' is required and is never inferred")
        mk2 = spec.get("mk2")
        bounds, vertices = _as_coordinates(kind, name, spec.get("coords"))
        gate = Gate(
            name=str(spec.get("filterId", name)),
            kind=kind,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            mk1=str(mk1),
            mk2=str(mk2) if mk2 else None,
            bounds=bounds,
            vertices=vertices,
        )
        gate.validate()
        gates.append(gate)

    channels: list[str] = []
    for gate in gates:
        for channel in gate.channels:
            if channel not in channels:
                channels.append(channel)
    return GateTable(gates=tuple(gates), channels=tuple(channels))
