docs.title: read_peacoqc_settings(path)
docs.text:
Read a PeacoQC settings file (YAML or JSON).

channels is required and is never inferred: PeacoQC's quality assessment is per-channel, and choosing the channels for someone is how a QC pass silently evaluates the wrong panel. The reference implementation's own spellings (:data:SETTINGS_ALIASES) are accepted so its 06_QC.yaml loads as written.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/peacoqc.py 
def read_peacoqc_settings(path: str | Path) -> PeacoQCSettings:
    """Read a PeacoQC settings file (YAML or JSON).

    ``channels`` is required and is never inferred: PeacoQC's quality assessment is
    per-channel, and choosing the channels for someone is how a QC pass silently
    evaluates the wrong panel.  The reference implementation's own spellings
    (:data:`SETTINGS_ALIASES`) are accepted so its ``06_QC.yaml`` loads as written.
    """

    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        raise PeacoQCError(f"PeacoQC settings file not found: {p}")
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    raw = (
        json.loads(text) if p.suffix.lower() == ".json" else yaml_safe_load(text, p)
    )
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise PeacoQCError(f"{p}: top level must be a mapping")
    renamed: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in raw.items():
        name = SETTINGS_ALIASES.get(str(key), str(key))
        if name in renamed:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                f"{p}: setting {key!r} is a second spelling of {name!r}, which is also "
                "set. Two spellings of one setting can disagree, and the one that lost "
                "would be the one acted on"
            )
        renamed[name] = value
    if "channels" not in renamed:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"{p}: 'channels' is required and is never inferred. PeacoQC evaluates "
            "quality per channel, so an omitted list would mean the wrong panel"
        )
    known = set(PeacoQCSettings.__dataclass_fields__)
    unknown = sorted(set(renamed) - known)
    if unknown:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"{p}: unknown setting(s) {unknown}; expected a subset of {sorted(known)}. A "
            "setting this build does not read would be accepted and then ignored"
        )
    return PeacoQCSettings(**renamed)

docs.text:
Run PeacoQC per sample and return every event it removed, with the reason.

One FCS file per sample is written, carrying :data:IDENTITY_CHANNEL, because PeacoQC's audited interface is a flowFrame and a flowFrame is what flowCore::read.FCS returns. The file is read back to resolve PeacoQC's row indices into the caller's own event indices, so nothing here depends on row order surviving by luck.

Raises :class:PeacoQCNotAvailable when R or PeacoQC is missing, and :class:PeacoQCError when PeacoQC ran but the result cannot be trusted. Neither is ever reported as "no events were removed".

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/peacoqc.py 
def run_peacoqc(
    values: np.ndarray,
    channels: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    sample_ids: np.ndarray,
    original_event_index: np.ndarray,
    settings: PeacoQCSettings,
    work_dir: str | Path,
    rscript: str = "Rscript",
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> PeacoQCResult:
    """Run PeacoQC per sample and return every event it removed, with the reason.

    One FCS file per sample is written, carrying :data:`IDENTITY_CHANNEL`, because
    PeacoQC's audited interface is a ``flowFrame`` and a flowFrame is what
    ``flowCore::read.FCS`` returns.  The file is read back to resolve PeacoQC's row
    indices into the caller's own event indices, so nothing here depends on row order
    surviving by luck.

    Raises :class:`PeacoQCNotAvailable` when R or PeacoQC is missing, and
    :class:`PeacoQCError` when PeacoQC ran but the result cannot be trusted.  Neither is
    ever reported as "no events were removed".
    """

    # The call is validated BEFORE anything is looked up on PATH.  A malformed call is
    # wrong in every environment; reporting "no R on PATH" for one would hide the defect
    # behind an environment fact, and the no-R path is already covered by
    # rscript="Rscript-does-not-exist".
    if IDENTITY_CHANNEL in {str(c).upper() for c in channels}:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"the channel {IDENTITY_CHANNEL!r} is reserved for the event-identity check "
            "and collides with a channel PeacoQC was asked to evaluate; rename it"
        )
    if not settings.channels:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            "no channel was named for PeacoQC to evaluate; a QC call over an empty "
            "channel list removes nothing and reports success"
        )
    missing = [c for c in settings.channels if c not in set(channels)]
    if missing:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"PeacoQC was asked to evaluate channel(s) {missing}, which the data does not "
            "carry. A missing channel is not a quiet one: PeacoQC would evaluate whatever "
            "was closest or fail on a channel mismatch"
        )

    work = Path(work_dir)
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    in_dir = work / "fcs_in"
    samples = np.asarray(sample_ids).astype(str)
    event_index = np.asarray(original_event_index).astype(np.int64)
    if samples.shape[0] != values.shape[0] or event_index.shape[0] != values.shape[0]:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"values has {values.shape[0]} rows but sample_ids has {samples.shape[0]} and "
            f"original_event_index has {event_index.shape[0]}; the three must be row-aligned"
        )

    if not r_available(rscript):
        raise PeacoQCNotAvailable(
            f"{rscript!r} is not on PATH, so PeacoQC cannot run. This build does not "
            "substitute another quality-control algorithm for it"
        )
    probe = r_package_version("PeacoQC", rscript)
    if not probe.available:
        raise PeacoQCNotAvailable(
            "the PeacoQC R package is not installed in this environment "
            f"({probe.detail}). Install bioconductor-peacoqc; scripts/setup_r_env.sh "
            "lists it"
        )

    file_of_sample: dict[str, str] = {}
    for sample_id in sorted(set(samples)):
        rows = np.flatnonzero(samples == sample_id)
        if rows.size == 0:  # pragma: no cover - set() came from samples
            continue
        ordered = rows[np.argsort(event_index[rows], kind="stable")]
        index = event_index[ordered].astype(np.float64)
        block = np.column_stack([index, np.asarray(values[ordered], dtype=np.float64)])
        path = write_fcs(
            in_dir / f"{sample_id}.fcs",
            block,
            [IDENTITY_CHANNEL, *[str(c) for c in channels]],
            [IDENTITY_CHANNEL, *[str(c) for c in channels]],
            scale="raw instrument units, as handed to the QC step",
            processing_note=(
                "batchdx-cyto per-sample file for PeacoQC; values are exactly as loaded, "
                f"carrying the original event index in {IDENTITY_CHANNEL} so the removal "
                "index can be resolved back to the baseline"
            ),
            source_sample=sample_id,
            extra_keywords={"BATCHDX_PURPOSE": "peacoqc_input"},
            overwrite=True,
        )
        file_of_sample[sample_id] = str(path)

    params = settings.to_params(work / "peacoqc_out")
    ordered = sorted(file_of_sample)
    # The R script keys its results by SAMPLE ID, sent explicitly rather than derived
    # from a file name. Deriving it would make the two sides disagree by an extension on
    # the one field the removal log is built from. Two parallel character vectors rather
    # than a list of records, because jsonlite's simplifyVector collapses a list of
    # objects into a data frame.
    params["sample_ids"] = list(ordered)
    params["files"] = [file_of_sample[sid] for sid in ordered]
    try:
        r_result = run_r_script(
            R_SCRIPT, params, work, rscript=rscript,
            log_path=work / "peacoqc.log", timeout=timeout,
        )
    except RNotAvailable as exc:  # pragma: no cover - checked above
        raise PeacoQCNotAvailable(str(exc)) from exc
    except RScriptFailed as exc:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"the PeacoQC script failed: {exc}. Last lines of the R log:\n"
            f"{exc.log[-2000:]}"
        ) from exc

    payload = r_result.payload
    if payload.get("status") != "ok":
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"the PeacoQC script did not report success: {payload.get('status')!r} "
            f"{payload.get('reason', '')}".strip()
        )
    per_file = payload.get("samples")
    if not isinstance(per_file, dict) or not per_file:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            "the PeacoQC script returned no per-sample result; an empty result is not a "
            "result in which nothing was removed"
        )
    absent = sorted(set(file_of_sample) - set(per_file))
    if absent:
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"the PeacoQC script returned no entry for sample(s) {absent}; a sample that "
            "was not assessed is not a sample that passed"
        )

    reason = settings.reason
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    outcomes: list[SampleQCOutcome] = []
    for sample_id, path in file_of_sample.items():
        entry = per_file[sample_id]
        n_input = int(entry.get("n_input", 0))
        good = _as_list(entry.get("good_cells"))
        if len(good) != n_input:
            raise PeacoQCError(
                f"PeacoQC returned {len(good)} per-cell decisions for sample "
                f"{sample_id!r}, which had {n_input} events. A decision vector of the "
                "wrong length cannot be mapped to events and is refused rather than "
                "truncated or padded"
            )
        if "GoodCells" not in entry.get("result_keys", []):
            raise PeacoQCError(
                f"PeacoQC's result for sample {sample_id!r} has no 'GoodCells' element; "
                f"it has {entry.get('result_keys')}. The removal index is derived from "
                "!GoodCells, and on a version without it nothing here can say which events "
                "were removed"
            )
        keep = np.array([bool(g) for g in good], dtype=bool)
        removed_rows = np.flatnonzero(~keep)
        # One read of the file serves both purposes: it proves the identity channel
        # survived the round trip, and it is what the removal positions are resolved
        # against. Skipping the read when nothing was removed would leave the "PeacoQC
        # looked at the file we think it looked at" claim untested in exactly the case a
        # reader would want it most (a clean sample).
        written_index = _read_identity_channel(path, sample_id)
        removed_index = (
            np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
            if removed_rows.size == 0
            else written_index[removed_rows]
        )

        if removed_index.size:
            frames.append(
                removal_frame(
                    sample_id=[sample_id] * removed_index.size,
                    original_event_index=removed_index,
                    step=STEP_QC,
                    reason=reason,
                )
            )
        it_fraction = _as_float_or_none(entry.get("it_fraction"))
        mad_fraction = _as_float_or_none(entry.get("mad_fraction"))
        it_available = bool(entry.get("it_available", False))
        it_reason = entry.get("it_reason")
        applied: list[str] = []
        if it_fraction is not None and it_fraction >= 0:
            applied.append("IT")
        if mad_fraction is not None and mad_fraction >= 0:
            applied.append("MAD")
        notes: list[str] = []
        if not it_available:
            notes.append(
                "the isolation-tree analysis did not run"
                + (f" ({it_reason})" if it_reason else "")
                + f", so determine_good_cells={settings.criteria!r} was decided on "
                + ("MAD alone" if applied == ["MAD"] else "no criterion")
                + ". This is a MAD-only pass recorded as such, not the 'all' that was "
                "requested"
            )
        pct = _as_float_or_none(entry.get("percentage_removed"))
        outcomes.append(
            SampleQCOutcome(
                sample_id=sample_id,
                n_input=n_input,
                n_removed=int(removed_index.size),
                removed_fraction=pct,
                it_fraction=it_fraction,
                mad_fraction=mad_fraction,
                criteria_applied=tuple(applied),
                it_available=it_available,
                it_reason=str(it_reason) if it_reason else None,
                notes=tuple(notes),
            )
        )

    removed = (
        pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
        if frames
        else pd.DataFrame(columns=["sample_id", "original_event_index", "step", "reason"])
    )
    if len(removed) != int(sum(o.n_removed for o in outcomes)):
        raise PeacoQCError(
            f"the removal log holds {len(removed)} rows but the per-sample outcomes "
            f"report {int(sum(o.n_removed for o in outcomes))} removals; the two are "
            "derived from one call and must agree"
        )
    return PeacoQCResult(
        removed=removed,
        samples=tuple(outcomes),
        software=tuple(peacoqc_availability(rscript)),
        warnings=tuple(str(w) for w in _as_list(payload.get("warnings"))),
        status="ok",
        report_paths={sid: str(entry.get("report_path") or "") for sid, entry in per_file.items()},
        output_files={
            sid: [str(f) for f in _as_list(entry.get("output_files"))]
            for sid, entry in per_file.items()
        },
    )

def settings_from_config(config, base_dir: str | Path = ".") -> PeacoQCSettings | None:
    """The settings ``preprocessing.peacoqc`` declares, or ``None`` if it declares none.

    This is the reader that makes ``preprocessing.peacoqc`` a key rather than a promise.
    It reads the key and nothing else: the channels come from the settings file and are
    never taken from the panel, because PeacoQC's assessment is per-channel and choosing
    the channels for someone is how a QC pass silently evaluates the wrong panel.
    """

    declared = config.preprocessing.peacoqc
    if declared is None:
        return None
    return read_peacoqc_settings(Path(base_dir) / str(declared))

def check_removal_log(frame: pd.DataFrame, *, what: str = "removal log") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Validate a log's columns, step names and dtypes, and return it normalised.

    Returns a copy with the dtypes the rest of the package assumes, so that a log read
    from a file and one built in memory behave identically.
    """

    if not isinstance(frame, pd.DataFrame):
        raise RemovalLogError(f"{what}: expected a DataFrame, got {type(frame).__name__}")
    missing = [c for c in REMOVED_EVENT_COLUMNS if c not in frame.columns]
    if missing:
        raise RemovalLogError(
            f"{what}: missing column(s) {missing}; expected {REMOVED_EVENT_COLUMNS}"
        )
    extra = [c for c in frame.columns if c not in REMOVED_EVENT_COLUMNS]
    if extra:
        raise RemovalLogError(
            f"{what}: unexpected column(s) {extra}. A removal log that has grown columns "
            "nothing renders is a log that has started accumulating silently"
        )
    out = frame.loc[:, REMOVED_EVENT_COLUMNS].copy()
    out["sample_id"] = out["sample_id"].astype(str)
    out["original_event_index"] = (
        out["original_event_index"].astype(float).round().astype(np.int64)
    )
    unknown = sorted(set(out["step"]) - set(KNOWN_STEPS))
    if unknown:
        raise RemovalLogError(
            f"{what}: step label(s) {unknown} are not among {list(KNOWN_STEPS)}"
        )
    if (out["reason"].astype(str).str.strip() == "").any():
        raise RemovalLogError(f"{what}: at least one row has an empty reason")
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

docs.text:
Build one step's removal rows, with the dtypes the log declares.

original_event_index is cast to a signed integer and sample_id to a string, because a log read back from CSV would otherwise carry them as float64 and object respectively and every join against Dataset.obs would silently produce an empty frame rather than an error.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/removals.py 
def removal_frame(
    *,
    sample_id: np.ndarray | list,
    original_event_index: np.ndarray | list,
    step: str,
    reason: str,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build one step's removal rows, with the dtypes the log declares.

    ``original_event_index`` is cast to a signed integer and ``sample_id`` to a string,
    because a log read back from CSV would otherwise carry them as ``float64`` and
    ``object`` respectively and every join against ``Dataset.obs`` would silently
    produce an empty frame rather than an error.
    """

    if step not in KNOWN_STEPS:
        raise RemovalLogError(
            f"removal step {step!r} is not one this build names; expected one of "
            f"{list(KNOWN_STEPS)}. An uninterpretable step label is worse than none"
        )
    if not str(reason).strip():
        raise RemovalLogError(
            "a removal without a reason is not a record: say which criterion removed the "
            "event. 'it is missing from the output' is not a reason"
        )
    sample = np.asarray(sample_id).astype(str)
    index = np.asarray(original_event_index)
    if index.dtype.kind == "f":
        if not np.isfinite(index).all():
            raise RemovalLogError("original_event_index holds a non-finite value")
        index = np.rint(index)
    index = index.astype(np.int64)
    if sample.shape != index.shape:
        raise RemovalLogError(
            f"sample_id has {sample.shape[0]} entries and original_event_index has "
            f"{index.shape[0]}; the two must be row-aligned"
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "sample_id": sample,
            "original_event_index": index,
            "step": np.repeat(step, sample.shape[0]),
            "reason": np.repeat(str(reason), sample.shape[0]),
        },
        columns=REMOVED_EVENT_COLUMNS,
    )

This is the reported shape: a reader wants "how many events did each criterion remove, where", not the log itself. It is computed from the log, never assembled separately, so the two cannot disagree.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/removals.py 
def summarise_removals(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Removed-event counts per step, per reason and per sample.

    This is the *reported* shape: a reader wants "how many events did each criterion
    remove, where", not the log itself.  It is computed from the log, never assembled
    separately, so the two cannot disagree.
    """

    checked = check_removal_log(frame)
    if checked.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["step", "reason", "sample_id", "n_removed"])
    grouped = (
        checked.groupby(["step", "reason", "sample_id"], dropna=False)
        .size()
        .reset_index(name="n_removed")
    )
    return grouped.sort_values(["step", "reason", "sample_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)

The claim under test is that :func:asinh_invert and :meth:batchdx.cyto.io.export.InversionPlan.apply are the same function. A test that compared two literals in the same module would only prove the module is internally consistent, so this builds the exporter's own plan and calls its own method.

def agree_with_exporter_inverse(
    values: np.ndarray, cofactor: float, *, atol: float = 1e-9
) -> bool:
    """Execute the cross-check against the real exporter, not a copy of it.

    The claim under test is that :func:`asinh_invert` and
    :meth:`batchdx.cyto.io.export.InversionPlan.apply` are the same function.  A test
    that compared two literals in the same module would only prove the module is
    internally consistent, so this builds the exporter's own plan and calls its own
    method.
    """

    from batchdx.cyto.io.export import InversionPlan

    plan = InversionPlan(invertible=True, scale_label="cross-check", note="", cofactor=cofactor)
    exporter = plan.apply(np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64))
    return bool(np.allclose(exporter, asinh_invert(values, cofactor), rtol=0.0, atol=atol))

def asinh_invert(values: np.ndarray, cofactor: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """``sinh(x) * cofactor`` — the exact inverse of :func:`asinh_transform`."""

    c = _check_cofactor(cofactor)
    return np.sinh(np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)) * c

docs.text:
(max_absolute, max_relative) error of transform-then-invert.

A missing key is never a zero, so this returns the measured error rather than a boolean: a caller can state how exact the round trip was instead of asserting that it was.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/preprocess/transform.py 
def asinh_round_trip_error(
    values: np.ndarray, cofactor: float | np.ndarray
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """``(max_absolute, max_relative)`` error of transform-then-invert.

    A missing key is never a zero, so this returns the measured error rather than a
    boolean: a caller can state how exact the round trip was instead of asserting that
    it was.
    """

    c = _check_cofactor(cofactor)
    raw = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    if raw.size == 0:
        raise TransformError("cannot measure a round-trip error over an empty array")
    back = asinh_invert(asinh_transform(raw, c), c)
    delta = np.abs(back - raw)
    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(raw), 1.0)
    return float(delta.max()), float((delta / scale).max())

def asinh_transform(values: np.ndarray, cofactor: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """``asinh(raw / cofactor)`` — the convention :mod:`io.export` inverts exactly."""

    c = _check_cofactor(cofactor)
    return np.arcsinh(np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64) / c)

def resolve_convention(name: str) -> TransformConvention:
    """The named convention, or a refusal naming what this build does implement."""

    key = (name or "none").lower()
    if key == "none":
        raise TransformError(
            "no transformation was declared: the values are already in the coordinate "
            "system the processing manifest names, and there is nothing to apply"
        )
    if key not in CONVENTIONS:
        raise TransformError(
            f"transformation {name!r} is not implemented by this build; it implements "
            f"{sorted(CONVENTIONS)}"
        )
    return CONVENTIONS[key]

How badly the scaled asinh convention breaks this build's inverse.

Provided so the difference in item 3.2 is a number that a test asserts, rather than a claim in a comment. It is not a supported transform; it is the thing that must never be confused with :func:asinh_transform.

def scaled_asinh_mismatch(
    values: np.ndarray, cofactor: float
) -> float:
    """How badly the *scaled* asinh convention breaks this build's inverse.

    Provided so the difference in item 3.2 is a number that a test asserts, rather than
    a claim in a comment.  It is not a supported transform; it is the thing that must
    never be confused with :func:`asinh_transform`.
    """

    c = _check_cofactor(cofactor)
    raw = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    scaled = asinh_transform(raw, c) * c
    back = asinh_invert(scaled, c)
    return float((np.abs(back - raw) / np.maximum(np.abs(raw), 1.0)).max())

class Redactor:
    """Stable pseudonyms for identifiers, plus private-path stripping."""

    def __init__(self, enabled: bool = True, base_dir: str | Path = ".", salt: str = "batchdx"):
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.base = Path(base_dir).resolve()
        self.salt = salt
        self._map: dict[str, str] = {}

    def identifier(self, value: str | None, kind: str = "ID") -> str:
        if value is None:
            return ""
        if not self.enabled:
            return str(value)
        text = str(value)
        if text not in self._map:
            digest = hashlib.sha256((self.salt + "|" + text).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
            self._map[text] = f"{kind}-{digest}"
        return self._map[text]

    def strip_paths(self, obj):
        """Recursively replace path-like strings in a JSON-ready structure.

        Used on the resolved configuration before it is embedded in the report: input
        and checkout locations are private filesystem details and must not leak into a
        circulated document, whatever the 'identifiers redacted' pill promises.
        """

        if not self.enabled:
            return obj
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            return {k: self.strip_paths(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
        if isinstance(obj, list):
            return [self.strip_paths(v) for v in obj]
        if isinstance(obj, str):
            if obj.startswith(("/", "~/")) or (len(obj) > 2 and obj[1] == ":"):
                return self.path(obj)
        return obj

    def path(self, value: str | None) -> str:
        """Rewrite one path as ``<run>/…`` when it lies inside the run's own base.

        A relative path is resolved against ``base``, not against the process's working
        directory: a configuration is written relative to the project it describes, so
        ``data/preprocessed.h5ad`` means ``<project>/data/preprocessed.h5ad`` and would
        otherwise be resolved against whatever directory the report happened to be
        rendered from, which makes the same report redact differently on two machines.

        A path outside the base keeps its file name and loses everything above it, so
        the reader still learns which file was read and not which machine it came from.
        """

        if value is None:
            return ""
        text = str(value)
        if not text.strip():
            return text
        if not self.enabled:
            return text
        if text.startswith(("<redacted>", "<run>")):
            # Already a rewritten placeholder. Redacting it again would resolve it
            # against the base like a relative path and mangle it into
            # "<run>/<redacted>/...", so a placeholder passes through unchanged.
            return text
        candidate = Path(text).expanduser()
        if not candidate.is_absolute():
            candidate = self.base / candidate
        try:
            resolved = candidate.resolve()
        except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            return f"<redacted>/{candidate.name}"
        try:
            return str(Path("<run>") / resolved.relative_to(self.base))
        except ValueError:
            return f"<redacted>/{resolved.name}"

    def write_map(self, path: str | Path) -> Path | None:
        """Write the pseudonym mapping, or nothing when redaction is off."""

        if not self.enabled or not self._map:
            return None
        p = Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(
            json.dumps({"note": "keep this file separate from any circulated report",
                        "mapping": self._map}, indent=2) + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        return p

def render_report(
    config_path: str | Path,
    base_dir: str | Path,
    layout,
    diagnosis_only: bool = False,
) -> Path:
    """Render ``report.html``.  ``diagnosis_only`` renders before any correction exists."""

    config = load_config(config_path)
    redactor = Redactor(enabled=config.report.redact_identifiers, base_dir=base_dir,
                        salt=run_salt(layout.root))
    # When preprocessing is enabled the run's input is the frozen baseline, not the
    # raw file the configuration names: the report's figures are drawn from the same
    # matrix every other stage analysed, and the raw input's row count would not even
    # align with a corrected candidate's output.
    if config.preprocessing.enabled and layout.preprocess_baseline.exists():
        from batchdx.cyto.pipeline import _baseline_config

        dataset = load_dataset(_baseline_config(config, layout), base_dir)
    else:
        dataset = load_dataset(config, base_dir)

    design = DesignAudit.read(layout.design_audit)
    sampling = (
        SamplingManifest.read(layout.sampling_manifest)
        if layout.sampling_manifest.exists() else None
    )

    detectors: list[DetectorResult] = []
    for name in sorted({p.parent.name for p in
                        (layout.root / "diagnostics").glob("*/detector_result.json")}):
        detectors.append(DetectorResult.read(layout.detector_result(name)))

    corrections: dict[str, CorrectionResult] = {}
    metrics: dict[str, MetricResult] = {}
    if not diagnosis_only:
        for candidate in config.correction.candidates:
            cpath = layout.correction_result(candidate.id)
            if cpath.exists():
                corrections[candidate.id] = CorrectionResult.read(cpath)
            mpath = layout.metric_result(candidate.id)
            if mpath.exists():
                metrics[candidate.id] = MetricResult.read(mpath)

    decision = (
        DecisionResult.read(layout.decision)
        if (not diagnosis_only and layout.decision.exists()) else None
    )

    # The exports.* configuration is consumed here: when FCS export is requested,
    # every successful candidate's corrected matrix is written as one FCS per
    # sample under the run's exports directory. Nothing is exported by default.
    if config.exports.fcs and not diagnosis_only:
        from batchdx.cyto.io.dataset import write_candidate_output  # noqa: F401
        from batchdx.cyto.io.export import export_fcs_per_sample

        for candidate in config.correction.candidates:
            result_path = layout.correction_result(candidate.id)
            corrected = layout.corrected_h5ad(candidate.id)
            if not (result_path.exists() and corrected.exists()):
                continue
            result = CorrectionResult.read(result_path)
            if result.status is not CorrectionStatus.SUCCESS:
                continue
            import anndata as ad

            adata = ad.read_h5ad(corrected)
            layer_name = str(adata.uns.get("expression_layer", "corrected"))
            matrix = np.asarray(adata.layers[layer_name], dtype=np.float64)
            out_dir = layout.root / "exports" / candidate.id / "fcs"
            export_fcs_per_sample(
                dataset, matrix, out_dir, candidate_id=candidate.id, invert=True,
            )

    all_records: list[MetricRecord] = []
    for result in metrics.values():
        all_records.extend(result.records)
    if layout.reductions.exists():
        payload = json.loads(layout.reductions.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        all_records.extend(MetricRecord.model_validate(r) for r in payload["records"])

    metric_rows = _metric_rows(all_records)
    metric_columns = list(metric_rows[0]) if metric_rows else ["metric", "status"]

    # -- figures ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    batch_of = dataset.sample_batches()
    obs = dataset.obs
    evaluation_markers = list(
        sampling.evaluation_markers if sampling else dataset.marker_ids("evaluation")
    )
    markers, markers_omitted = _marker_selection(evaluation_markers, EXPLORER_MARKER_LIMIT)
    comparison_markers, comparison_omitted = _marker_selection(
        evaluation_markers, COMPARISON_MARKER_LIMIT
    )
    baseline = dataset.expression()
    figures: list[dict] = []
    for marker in markers:
        col = dataset.feature_index([marker])[0]
        by_batch: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for sid in obs[SAMPLE_ID].unique():
            batch = batch_of.get(str(sid))
            if batch is None:
                continue
            mask = (obs[SAMPLE_ID] == sid).to_numpy()
            by_batch.setdefault(str(batch), []).append(baseline[mask, col])
        merged = {b: np.concatenate(v) for b, v in by_batch.items()}
        figures.append({"title": marker, "svg": plots.density_by_batch(
            merged, f"{marker} by batch (uncorrected)", "expression")})

    comparison_figures: list[dict] = []
    corrected_matrices: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    if not diagnosis_only:
        import anndata as ad

        for candidate_id, result in sorted(corrections.items()):
            path = layout.corrected_h5ad(candidate_id)
            if result.status.value != "success" or not path.exists():
                continue
            adata = ad.read_h5ad(path)
            layer = str(adata.uns.get("expression_layer", "corrected"))
            corrected = np.asarray(adata.layers[layer], dtype=np.float64)
            corrected_matrices[candidate_id] = corrected
            for marker in comparison_markers:
                col = dataset.feature_index([marker])[0]
                before, after = {}, {}
                for batch in sorted({b for b in batch_of.values() if b}):
                    mask = obs[SAMPLE_ID].map(batch_of).to_numpy() == batch
                    before[batch] = baseline[mask, col]
                    after[batch] = corrected[mask, col]
                comparison_figures.append({
                    "candidate": candidate_id, "marker": marker,
                    "svg": plots.before_after(before, after, marker, "expression"),
                })

    composition_figure = None
    if sampling is not None:
        freq = frequency_table(dataset, sampling.labels_by_cell)
        composition_figure = plots.frequency_bars(
            {redactor.identifier(k, "S"): v for k, v in freq.items()},
            {redactor.identifier(k, "S"): (batch_of.get(k) or "") for k in freq},
        )

    # -- assembled context -----------------------------------------------------------
    samples = [{
        "sample_id": redactor.identifier(rec.sample_id, "S"),
        "donor_id": redactor.identifier(rec.donor_id, "D") if rec.donor_id else "",
        "batch": rec.batch or "",
        "group": rec.group or "",
        "stimulation": rec.stimulation or "",
        "timepoint": rec.timepoint or "",
        "reference_id": redactor.identifier(rec.reference_id, "R") if rec.reference_id else "",
        "reference_role": str(rec.reference_role),
        "n_cells": rec.n_cells or 0,
    } for rec in dataset.manifest.samples]

    # Every identifier the run knows, so a detector's or a metric's free text can be
    # scrubbed against the same set the samples table was redacted with.  Collected after
    # ``samples`` so every one of them already has a pseudonym.
    known_ids = frozenset(
        str(value)
        for rec in dataset.manifest.samples
        for value in (rec.sample_id, rec.donor_id, rec.reference_id)
        if value
    )
    metric_rows = _scrub_metric_reasons(metric_rows, redactor, known_ids)

    failures = []
    for result in detectors:
        if result.status != "ok":
            failures.append({
                "kind": "detector", "unit": result.detector, "status": result.status,
                "reason": _redact_free_form(result.reason, redactor, known_ids)
                if result.reason else "",
            })
    for candidate_id, result in sorted(corrections.items()):
        if result.status.value != "success":
            failures.append({
                "kind": "candidate", "unit": candidate_id, "status": result.status.value,
                "reason": _redact_free_form(result.reason, redactor, known_ids)
                if result.reason else "",
            })
    for record in all_records:
        if record.status in (MetricStatus.FAILED, MetricStatus.NOT_IMPLEMENTED):
            failures.append({
                "kind": "metric", "unit": record.metric_name, "status": str(record.status),
                "reason": _redact_free_form(record.reason, redactor, known_ids)
                if record.reason else "",
            })

    joint_rows = [
        r for r in metric_rows if r["metric"] == "joint_structure_distance"
    ]

    detector_views = _detector_views(detectors, redactor, known_ids)

    context = {
        "title": config.report.title,
        "version": __version__,
        "diagnosis_only": diagnosis_only,
        "config": _redact_config_paths(
            redactor.strip_paths(config.resolved_dict()), redactor
        ),
        "fingerprint": config.analytical_fingerprint(),
        "dataset": dataset.manifest,
        "processing": dataset.processing,
        "samples": samples,
        "design": design,
        "sampling": sampling,
        "detectors": detector_views,
        "corrections": corrections,
        "correction_rows": _correction_rows(corrections, redactor, known_ids),
        "decision": decision,
        "metric_rows": metric_rows,
        "metric_columns": metric_columns,
        "metric_csv": _data_uri_csv(metric_rows, metric_columns),
        "figures": figures,
        "explorer_markers": markers,
        "explorer_markers_total": len(evaluation_markers),
        "explorer_markers_omitted": markers_omitted,
        "comparison_markers": comparison_markers,
        "comparison_markers_omitted": comparison_omitted,
        "comparison_figures": comparison_figures,
        "composition_figure": composition_figure,
        "embedding_section": _embedding_view(dataset, corrected_matrices),
        "narrative": _narrative(decision, detector_views, len(all_records)),
        "preprocess_section": (
            _preprocess_view(layout) if config.preprocessing.enabled else None
        ),
        "joint_rows": joint_rows[:JOINT_ROW_LIMIT],
        "joint_note": _shown(len(joint_rows), JOINT_ROW_LIMIT),
        "failures": failures,
        "registered_metrics": sorted(
            (f"{ns}.{name}", spec) for (ns, name), spec in registered_metrics().items()
        ),
        "deferred_metrics": DEFERRED_METRICS,
        "upstream_not_found": UPSTREAM_METRICS_NOT_FOUND,
        "redacted": config.report.redact_identifiers,
        "parameter_list_limit": PARAMETER_LIST_LIMIT,
    }

    env = Environment(
        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(templates_root())),
        autoescape=select_autoescape(["html"]),
    )
    html = env.get_template("report.html.j2").render(**context)

    out = layout.report
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
    redactor.write_map(out.parent / "identifier_map.json")
    return out

docs.title: build_sampling_manifest(dataset, config, design, labels, label_tier, label_confidence)
docs.text:
Deterministic, sample-balanced evaluation cells plus the frozen comparison set.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/sampling/partitions.py 
def build_sampling_manifest(
    dataset: Dataset,
    config: Config,
    design: DesignAudit,
    labels: np.ndarray,
    label_tier: LabelTier,
    label_confidence: str,
) -> SamplingManifest:
    """Deterministic, sample-balanced evaluation cells plus the frozen comparison set."""

    if config.evaluation.partitions != FROZEN_COMMON:
        # Unreachable through parse_config, which pins the value.  Kept so that
        # widening the schema without widening this module fails loudly here instead
        # of quietly building the frozen partition under a name that promises another.
        raise PartitionError(
            f"evaluation.partitions={config.evaluation.partitions!r} is not implemented; "
            f"this build only builds the {FROZEN_COMMON!r} partition"
        )
    unit = config.evaluation.sampling.unit
    if unit != SAMPLE_SAMPLING_UNIT:
        # Likewise pinned by the schema.  The draw below is per sample, and the frozen
        # manifest records per-sample counts and weights, so honouring any other unit
        # would mean emitting a manifest that misdescribes the selection.
        raise PartitionError(
            f"evaluation.sampling.unit={unit!r} is not implemented; the evaluation draw is "
            f"balanced per {SAMPLE_SAMPLING_UNIT!r} and the frozen manifest records "
            f"per-sample counts, so no other unit can be recorded truthfully"
        )

    obs = dataset.obs
    obs["_label"] = labels
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.project.seed)

    cap = config.evaluation.sampling.max_cells_per_sample
    selected: list[str] = []
    per_sample: dict[str, int] = {}
    original: dict[str, int] = {}

    for sid in sorted(obs[SAMPLE_ID].unique()):
        block = obs.loc[obs[SAMPLE_ID] == sid]
        original[sid] = int(len(block))
        ids = block[CELL_ID].to_numpy()
        if cap is not None and len(ids) > cap:
            # Sort first so the draw depends only on the seed and the cell ids, never
            # on row order in the input file.
            ids = np.sort(ids)
            ids = ids[np.sort(rng.choice(len(ids), size=cap, replace=False))]
        else:
            ids = np.sort(ids)
        per_sample[sid] = int(len(ids))
        selected.extend(ids.tolist())

    selected_set = set(selected)
    sel = obs.loc[obs[CELL_ID].isin(selected_set)]
    labels_by_cell = dict(zip(sel[CELL_ID].tolist(), sel["_label"].astype(str).tolist(),
                              strict=True))
    population_counts = sel["_label"].astype(str).value_counts().to_dict()

    warnings: list[str] = []
    min_cells = config.evaluation.sampling.min_cells_per_population
    for pop, n in sorted(population_counts.items()):
        if n < min_cells:
            warnings.append(
                f"population {pop!r} has {n} evaluation cells overall, below the declared "
                f"minimum of {min_cells}; metrics for it will report insufficient_data"
            )
    if UNGATED in population_counts:
        warnings.append(
            f"{population_counts[UNGATED]} evaluation cell(s) matched no gate and are "
            f"labelled {UNGATED!r}; they are reported, never silently dropped"
        )

    batch_of = {sid: rec.batch for sid, rec in dataset.samples.items()}
    per_batch_pop: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
    for _, row in sel.iterrows():
        b = batch_of.get(str(row[SAMPLE_ID]))
        if b is not None:
            key = (b, str(row["_label"]))
            per_batch_pop[key] = per_batch_pop.get(key, 0) + 1
    for pop in sorted(population_counts):
        absent = [b for b in design.batches if per_batch_pop.get((b, pop), 0) == 0]
        if absent:
            warnings.append(
                f"population {pop!r} has no evaluation cells in batch(es) {absent}; "
                "comparisons involving those batches are unsupported for this population"
            )

    # A declared uncertainty unit is not a computed one.  Saying so here means the
    # report cannot be read as claiming donor-level uncertainty it never produced:
    # uncertainty_low/uncertainty_high/uncertainty_kind are null on every record.
    if config.evaluation.uncertainty_unit is not None:
        warnings.append(
            f"evaluation.uncertainty_unit={config.evaluation.uncertainty_unit!r} is recorded, "
            "but no unit-level uncertainty is computed in this build: the "
            "uncertainty_low/uncertainty_high/uncertainty_kind fields of every metric record "
            "are null, because donor-level uncertainty belongs to Stage 8 biological "
            "preservation, which is not implemented"
        )

    pairs = [
        (c.batch_a, c.batch_b)
        for c in design.comparisons
        if c.population is None and c.support is not ComparisonSupport.NON_IDENTIFIABLE
    ]

    # Biospecimen-level train/tune/validate.  Resolved from the same manifest seed
    # and the same frozen sample set, so a candidate cannot obtain a different
    # partition by being run in a different order.
    #
    # require_all_arms=False here, deliberately.  This manifest also serves the
    # detectors, the metrics and the report, and a design whose thinner arm holds
    # fewer biospecimens than there are splits is a reason to warn about the split,
    # not a reason to refuse to run: refusing would take the whole package down for a
    # limitation of one partition.  The deficiency is not hidden -- it becomes a
    # coverage warning rendered on the report -- and batchdx.cyto.sampling.splits
    # exposes missing_arms() so any consumer that must not use an unbalanced split
    # (notably the fit-and-apply CytoNorm backend) can refuse it.  A deficiency the
    # allocator could have fixed still raises, because that one is a defect.
    proportions = config.evaluation.sampling.split_proportions
    if proportions is None:
        proportion_origin = SPLIT_PROPORTION_ORIGIN
    else:
        proportion_origin = (
            "declared in the run configuration at evaluation.sampling.split_proportions; "
            "these user-configured shares replace the package default and are recorded "
            "here so a reader can disagree with them explicitly rather than inherit them"
        )
    assignment = build_splits(
        dataset.samples, donor_factor=config.design.donor, seed=config.project.seed,
        proportions=proportions, require_all_arms=False,
    )
    warnings.extend(assignment.warnings)

    rep = config.evaluation.representation
    representation = RepresentationSettings(
        space=rep.space, marker_mask=rep.marker_mask, scaling=rep.scaling,
        distance=rep.distance, k=rep.k,
    )

    # Equal weight per sample: a summary must not be dominated by whichever sample
    # happened to yield the most cells.
    weights = {sid: 1.0 for sid in per_sample}

    return SamplingManifest(
        dataset_id=dataset.manifest.dataset_id,
        seed=config.project.seed,
        unit=unit,
        max_cells_per_sample=cap,
        label_source=label_tier,
        label_confidence=label_confidence,
        label_column=config.evaluation.labels or "_batchdx_label",
        labels_by_cell=labels_by_cell,
        selected_cell_ids=sorted(selected_set),
        per_sample_counts=per_sample,
        per_sample_original_counts=original,
        population_counts={k: int(v) for k, v in population_counts.items()},
        population_coverage_warnings=warnings,
        comparison_pairs=pairs,
        evaluation_markers=dataset.marker_ids(rep.marker_mask),
        representation=representation,
        aggregation_weights=weights,
        splits=assignment.to_manifest(),
        split_proportions=dict(assignment.proportions),
        split_proportion_origin=proportion_origin,
        provenance=[ProvenanceRef(kind="dataset", identifier=dataset.manifest.dataset_id,
                                  content_hash=dataset.baseline_hash())],
    )

docs.text:
Read the threshold table.

Thresholds are fixed in the declared coordinate system before any candidate runs, and the same numbers are used before and after correction. There is no per-candidate retuning, because five experienced analysts setting five different thresholds for the same marker is a documented failure mode.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/sampling/partitions.py 
def read_gating_thresholds(path: str | Path) -> list[GatingRule]:
    """Read the threshold table.

    Thresholds are fixed in the declared coordinate system *before* any candidate
    runs, and the same numbers are used before and after correction.  There is no
    per-candidate retuning, because five experienced analysts setting five different
    thresholds for the same marker is a documented failure mode.
    """

    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        raise PartitionError(f"gating threshold table not found: {p}")
    sep = "," if p.suffix.lower() == ".csv" else "\t"
    df = pd.read_csv(p, sep=sep)
    required = {"population", "feature_id", "sign", "threshold"}
    missing = required - set(df.columns)
    if missing:
        raise PartitionError(f"{p}: missing column(s) {sorted(missing)}")
    rules: list[GatingRule] = []
    for i, row in df.iterrows():
        sign = str(row["sign"]).strip()
        if sign not in {"+", "-"}:
            raise PartitionError(f"{p} row {i}: sign must be '+' or '-', got {sign!r}")
        rules.append(GatingRule(
            population=str(row["population"]).strip(),
            feature_id=str(row["feature_id"]).strip(),
            sign=sign,
            threshold=float(row["threshold"]),
            priority=int(row["priority"]) if "priority" in df.columns else i,
        ))
    return rules

def resolve_labels(
    dataset: Dataset, config: Config, base_dir: str | Path = "."
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, LabelTier, str]:
    """Return frozen evaluation labels with their tier and confidence."""

    source = LabelTier(config.evaluation.label_source)
    if source is LabelTier.ANNOTATION:
        column = config.evaluation.labels
        if column not in dataset.adata.obs.columns:
            raise PartitionError(
                f"evaluation.labels column {column!r} is not present in the data; "
                "annotation labels are never invented"
            )
        labels = dataset.adata.obs[column].astype(str).to_numpy()
    elif source is LabelTier.GATING:
        rules = read_gating_thresholds(Path(base_dir) / config.evaluation.gating_thresholds)
        labels = _labels_from_gating(dataset, rules)
    else:
        labels = _labels_from_clustering(
            dataset, config.evaluation.clustering_k, config.project.seed
        )
    return labels, source, LABEL_TIER_CONFIDENCE[source]

class DatasetManifest(_Contract):
    """Immutable description of the preprocessed baseline used by every candidate."""

    dataset_id: str
    n_cells: int
    n_features: int
    expression_layer: str
    samples: list[SampleRecord]
    markers: list[MarkerRecord]
    processing: ProcessingManifest
    cell_index_columns: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: ["cell_id", "sample_id", "source_checksum", "original_event_index"]
    )
    baseline_hash: str | None = None
    provenance: list[ProvenanceRef] = Field(default_factory=list)

    def marker_ids(self, mask: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Feature ids, optionally restricted to one of the three declared masks."""
        attr = {"clustering": "use_for_clustering",
                "correction": "use_for_correction",
                "evaluation": "use_for_evaluation"}
        if mask is None:
            return [m.feature_id for m in self.markers]
        if mask not in attr:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown marker mask {mask!r}; expected one of {sorted(attr)}")
        return [m.feature_id for m in self.markers if getattr(m, attr[mask])]

    """Write one JSON Schema per contract, for validation from R or any other reader."""

docs.title: batchdx.cyto.simulate
docs.text:
Deterministic synthetic cytometry datasets used by examples and by the test suite.

The generator is a fixture, not a scientific claim. It produces a mixture of lineage populations with declared marker means, then applies separately controllable technical and biological perturbations so that a test can state exactly which effect it expects a method or metric to see.

The seed defaults here are :data:batchdx.cyto.config.DEFAULT_SEED, the same value :attr:batchdx.cyto.config.ProjectConfig.seed carries. A run's seed therefore has one source, and a fixture built with an explicit seed is the same seed the run records.

@dataclass
class SimulationSpec:
    """Full description of a synthetic dataset."""

    samples: list[SampleSpec]
    seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED
    sd: float = 0.35
    #: Strength of a shared per-cell latent factor within each population.  Real
    #: cytometry markers co-vary within a cell type (cell size, staining index,
    #: activation state); without that the joint-structure metric would have nothing
    #: to measure and a joint-destroying corruption would be undetectable by
    #: construction rather than by the metric working.
    within_population_correlation: float = 0.6
    #: batch -> marker -> additive shift on the declared scale (a technical offset)
    batch_shift: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    #: batch -> marker -> multiplicative spread factor (a technical dispersion change)
    batch_spread: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    #: group -> marker -> additive shift (a genuine biological difference)
    group_shift: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    #: sample -> marker -> shift accumulated linearly across acquisition order
    drift: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    populations: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: {k: dict(v) for k, v in DEFAULT_POPULATIONS.items()}
    )
    frequencies: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(DEFAULT_FREQUENCIES))
    scale: str = "asinh_cofactor5"

docs.title: simulate(spec)
docs.text:
Generate an AnnData plus the sample, marker and processing manifests.

The real expression matrix is written to adata.X and to the declared preprocessed layer. An earlier build wrote zeros to X on the grounds that the declared layer is the only source of truth; that zero was a trap for any generic AnnData reader of the fixture, so it is gone. Within this package the declared layer remains the source of truth (:meth:batchdx.cyto.io.dataset.Dataset.expression reads it and nothing reads X).

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/simulate.py 
def simulate(spec: SimulationSpec) -> tuple[ad.AnnData, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Generate an AnnData plus the sample, marker and processing manifests.

    The real expression matrix is written to ``adata.X`` *and* to the declared
    ``preprocessed`` layer.  An earlier build wrote zeros to ``X`` on the grounds
    that the declared layer is the only source of truth; that zero was a trap for
    any generic AnnData reader of the fixture, so it is gone.  Within this package
    the declared layer remains the source of truth
    (:meth:`batchdx.cyto.io.dataset.Dataset.expression` reads it and nothing reads
    ``X``).
    """

    markers = LINEAGE_MARKERS + FUNCTIONAL_MARKERS
    rng = np.random.default_rng(spec.seed)

    blocks, obs_rows = [], []
    for sample in spec.samples:
        freqs = sample.frequencies or spec.frequencies
        pops = list(freqs)
        probs = np.array([freqs[p] for p in pops], dtype=float)
        probs = probs / probs.sum()
        counts = rng.multinomial(sample.n_cells, probs)

        values = np.zeros((sample.n_cells, len(markers)), dtype=np.float64)
        labels = np.empty(sample.n_cells, dtype=object)

        start = 0
        for pop, n in zip(pops, counts, strict=True):
            if n == 0:
                continue
            means = np.array([spec.populations[pop][m] for m in markers], dtype=float)
            rho = float(spec.within_population_correlation)
            shared = rng.normal(size=(n, 1))
            independent = rng.normal(size=(n, len(markers)))
            noise = rho * shared + np.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - rho * rho)) * independent
            block = means + spec.sd * noise
            values[start:start + n, :] = block
            labels[start:start + n] = pop
            start += n

        order = rng.permutation(sample.n_cells)
        values, labels = values[order], labels[order]

        for m_i, m in enumerate(markers):
            values[:, m_i] += spec.batch_shift.get(sample.batch, {}).get(m, 0.0)
            values[:, m_i] += spec.group_shift.get(sample.group, {}).get(m, 0.0)
            spread = spec.batch_spread.get(sample.batch, {}).get(m)
            if spread is not None:
                centre = values[:, m_i].mean()
                values[:, m_i] = centre + (values[:, m_i] - centre) * spread
            slope = spec.drift.get(sample.sample_id, {}).get(m)
            if slope is not None:
                values[:, m_i] += slope * np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, sample.n_cells)

        blocks.append(values)
        obs_rows.append(pd.DataFrame({
            "sample_id": np.repeat(sample.sample_id, sample.n_cells),
            "original_event_index": np.arange(sample.n_cells, dtype=int),
            "acquisition_order": np.arange(sample.n_cells, dtype=int),
            "true_population": labels,
        }))

    X = np.vstack(blocks)
    obs = pd.concat(obs_rows, ignore_index=True)
    # X carries the same values as the declared "preprocessed" layer.  The declared
    # layer stays the source of truth for this package, but a zero X in a fixture is
    # not a convention, it is a footgun for every external reader.
    adata = ad.AnnData(
        X=X.astype(np.float32),
        obs=obs,
        var=pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index(markers, dtype=object)),
    )
    adata.layers["preprocessed"] = X

    sample_table = pd.DataFrame([{
        "sample_id": s.sample_id,
        "donor_id": s.donor_id,
        "biospecimen_id": f"{s.donor_id}_{s.timepoint}",
        "batch": s.batch,
        "group": s.group,
        "stimulation": s.stimulation,
        "timepoint": s.timepoint,
        "reference_id": s.reference_id or "",
        "reference_role": s.reference_role,
    } for s in spec.samples])

    marker_table = pd.DataFrame([{
        "feature_id": m,
        "channel": f"Ch_{m}",
        "marker": m,
        "panel_id": "panelA",
        "role": "lineage" if m in LINEAGE_MARKERS else "functional",
        "use_for_clustering": m in LINEAGE_MARKERS,
        "use_for_correction": True,
        "use_for_evaluation": True,
    } for m in markers])

    processing = {
        "compensated": True,
        "unmixed": False,
        "compensation_source": "simulated; no instrument spillover applied",
        "qc_history": ["simulated data: no QC performed"],
        "transformation": "asinh",
        "transformation_parameters": {"cofactor": 5.0},
        "scale": spec.scale,
        "units": "arcsinh units",
        "corrected": False,
        "notes": "synthetic fixture produced by batchdx.cyto.simulate",
    }
    return adata, sample_table, marker_table, processing

def write_simulation(spec: SimulationSpec, out_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write a simulated dataset and its manifests into ``out_dir``."""

    out = Path(out_dir)
    (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "config").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    adata, sample_table, marker_table, processing = simulate(spec)
    paths = {
        "h5ad": out / "data" / "preprocessed.h5ad",
        "samples": out / "config" / "samples.tsv",
        "markers": out / "config" / "markers.tsv",
        "processing": out / "config" / "processing.json",
    }
    adata.write_h5ad(paths["h5ad"])
    sample_table.to_csv(paths["samples"], sep="\t", index=False)
    marker_table.to_csv(paths["markers"], sep="\t", index=False)
    paths["processing"].write_text(json.dumps(processing, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return paths

docs.title: paired_reference_spec(seed=DEFAULT_SEED, n_cells=1500)
docs.text:
Three batches, a measured reference aliquot in each, balanced biology.

Batch B and C carry a technical offset on CD4 and HLADR; the biological difference between groups sits on CD69 and is present in every batch.

Source code in src/batchdx/cyto/simulate.py 
def paired_reference_spec(seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED, n_cells: int = 1500) -> SimulationSpec:
    """Three batches, a measured reference aliquot in each, balanced biology.

    Batch B and C carry a technical offset on CD4 and HLADR; the biological
    difference between groups sits on CD69 and is present in every batch.
    """

    samples: list[SampleSpec] = []
    for b_i, batch in enumerate(["B1", "B2", "B3"]):
        for ref in (("ref", "REFDONOR", "REF1"), ("ref2", "REFDONOR2", "REF2")):
            sid, donor, ref_id = ref
            samples.append(SampleSpec(
                sample_id=f"{sid}_{batch}", donor_id=donor, batch=batch, group="reference",
                reference_id=ref_id, reference_role="technical_replicate", n_cells=n_cells,
            ))
        for k in range(2):
            for group, tag in (("case", "CA"), ("control", "CO")):
                donor = f"D{b_i}{k}{tag}"
                samples.append(SampleSpec(
                    sample_id=f"{donor}_{batch}", donor_id=donor, batch=batch,
                    group=group, n_cells=n_cells,
                ))
    return SimulationSpec(
        samples=samples,
        seed=seed,
        batch_shift={"B2": {"CD4": 0.8, "HLADR": -0.5}, "B3": {"CD4": -0.6, "HLADR": 0.7}},
        group_shift={"case": {"CD69": 0.9}},
    )

def subtle_effect_spec(seed: int = 473, n_cells: int = 1500) -> SimulationSpec:
    """Batch shifts of 0.1-0.2 SD: 0.05-0.1 on the declared scale (sd = 0.35).

    The layout matches :func:`paired_reference_spec`, including the 0.9 biological
    case/control difference on CD69, but the technical offsets are an order of
    magnitude smaller.  A correction that removes these small offsets must leave the
    biological contrast in place, so a test can state a tolerance that is small
    relative to the biology yet large relative to the residual technical error.
    """

    samples: list[SampleSpec] = []
    for b_i, batch in enumerate(["B1", "B2", "B3"]):
        samples.append(SampleSpec(
            sample_id=f"ref_{batch}", donor_id="REFDONOR", batch=batch, group="reference",
            reference_id="REF1", reference_role="technical_replicate", n_cells=n_cells,
        ))
        for k in range(2):
            for group, tag in (("case", "CA"), ("control", "CO")):
                donor = f"D{b_i}{k}{tag}"
                samples.append(SampleSpec(
                    sample_id=f"{donor}_{batch}", donor_id=donor, batch=batch,
                    group=group, n_cells=n_cells,
                ))
    return SimulationSpec(
        samples=samples,
        seed=seed,
        batch_shift={
            "B2": {"CD4": 0.08, "HLADR": -0.06},
            "B3": {"CD4": -0.07, "HLADR": 0.09},

A fifth population below the 30-cell reporting floor in some samples.

Every sample devotes either 0.05% or 0.2% of its cells to the rare population (roughly one to three cells per 1500-cell sample), so every (population, batch) group and every group-level contrast sits far below the 30-cell minimum. Any metric that needs a minimum number of cells must report insufficient_data for this population, never a zero.

def rare_population_spec(seed: int = 473, n_cells: int = 1500) -> SimulationSpec:
    """A fifth population below the 30-cell reporting floor in some samples.

    Every sample devotes either 0.05% or 0.2% of its cells to the rare population
    (roughly one to three cells per 1500-cell sample), so every (population, batch)
    group and every group-level contrast sits far below the 30-cell minimum.  Any
    metric that needs a minimum number of cells must report ``insufficient_data``
    for this population, never a zero.
    """

    populations = {k: dict(v) for k, v in DEFAULT_POPULATIONS.items()}
    populations["Rare"] = {
        "CD3": 0.4, "CD4": 0.3, "CD8": 0.3, "CD19": 1.8, "CD14": 0.2, "CD56": 1.2,
        "HLADR": 2.4, "CD69": 0.9,
    }
    samples = []
    for b_i, batch in enumerate(["B1", "B2", "B3"]):
        for k in range(2):
            for group, tag in (("case", "CA"), ("control", "CO")):
                donor = f"D{b_i}{k}{tag}"
                freqs = dict(DEFAULT_FREQUENCIES)
                freqs["Rare"] = 0.0005 if (b_i + k) % 2 == 0 else 0.002
                samples.append(SampleSpec(
                    sample_id=f"{donor}_{batch}", donor_id=donor, batch=batch,
                    group=group, n_cells=n_cells, frequencies=freqs,
                ))
    return SimulationSpec(
        samples=samples,
        seed=seed,
        populations=populations,
        batch_shift={"B2": {"CD4": 0.8}, "B3": {"CD4": -0.6}},
        group_shift={"case": {"CD69": 0.9}},
    )

def confounded_spec(seed: int = 473, n_cells: int = 1500) -> SimulationSpec:
    """Two batches, perfectly confounded with biological group, no reference."""

    samples = []

docs.title: 0001 — The internal data contract is AnnData plus seven typed records
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Cytometry arrives as FCS or as AnnData/H5AD, and every downstream stage needs to agree on what a cell is, what a marker is, and what has already been done to the values.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
AnnData is the canonical logical interchange contract. The expression values live in a named layer that the configuration declares; X is never used implicitly.

Five manifests describe the data (cell index, sample, marker, processing, candidate), and seven versioned records cross every stage boundary: DatasetManifest, DesignAudit, SamplingManifest, DetectorResult, CorrectionResult, MetricResult, DecisionResult. They are pydantic models with extra="forbid" and a schema_version, and their JSON Schemas are exported for the R side (schemas/contracts.py::export_json_schemas).

The preprocessed baseline is immutable. Each correction candidate writes its own AnnData file; nothing accumulates candidates into one object.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A record written by a newer build fails loudly instead of being half-read.
  • Adding a field is a contract change and bumps CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION.
  • Memory cost: one baseline plus one candidate matrix at a time, not N candidates.

docs.title: 0002 — R runs in subprocesses, never embedded in the Python process
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: cyCombine, CytoNorm and CytoBatchFlagR are R. The obvious alternative is an embedded interpreter (rpy2), which puts a second garbage-collected runtime inside the analysis process and turns an upstream segfault into a lost run.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Every R call is Rscript --vanilla workflow/scripts/<name>.R params.json result.json in a subprocess. Inputs and outputs cross as JSON plus a typed binary matrix (io/binary.py and workflow/scripts/lib/binmat.R: raw little-endian float64 with a JSON sidecar carrying shape, row ids and column names).

The binary format uses base R's readBin only, so the exchange adds no R package dependency of its own beyond jsonlite.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An R failure is a non-zero exit status plus a captured log, never a corrupted in-process state; RScriptFailed carries the log into the CorrectionResult.
  • No large delimited-text intermediates.
  • Cost: one process spawn and one matrix round trip per call. Acceptable, because the R side is doing minutes of work, not milliseconds.

docs.title: 0003 — CytoBatchFlagR is invoked at arm's length, never vendored
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0). This decision is a licence decision and was recorded before the adapter was written.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
CytoBatchFlagR (published 2026 in Cytometry Part A; first released as cytoFlagR, bioRxiv 2025) is distributed as R scripts, not as an installable package: the checkout at the pinned commit has no DESCRIPTION and no NAMESPACE. Its entry point R/CytoBatchFlagR_workflow.R is interactive — it calls rstudioapi::selectDirectory and several Shiny helpers.

The repository carries GPL-3.0. batchdx-cyto is MIT.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Integrate at arm's length:

  1. The user supplies a checkout at the commit pinned in config/upstream_lock.yaml (scripts/fetch_upstream.sh fetches it).
  2. workflow/scripts/cytobatchflagr_detect.R source()s R/CytoBatchFlagR_functions.R unmodified, in a separate R process.
  3. The interactive workflow script is deliberately not sourced. The analysis functions (neg_mfi_df_all, pos_mfi_df_all, percent_pos_df_all, iqr_dataframe) are called directly with values taken from configuration: directories, marker selections, reference identities and thresholds.
  4. No upstream source is copied into this package and none is refactored.

Refactoring upstream into a package — the obvious engineering improvement — would create a derivative work and is therefore out of scope for an MIT distribution. If that becomes necessary, the correct route is a separate GPL-3 package, not a change here.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The adapter reports not_available with an explicit reason when no checkout is present, rather than failing obscurely or fabricating flags.
  • The three IQR metrics require a control sample in every batch; that constraint, and the arithmetic fact that the 1.5 IQR fence cannot fire for n <= 3 batches, are encoded in the Stage 3 eligibility manifest with their origin stated.
  • Thresholds must be supplied. The publication reports five experienced analysts choosing five different thresholds for the same markers, so the adapter refuses to pick them itself.

docs.title: 0004 — Upstream R packages are pinned by commit and need a container
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: cyCombine and CytoNorm are distributed through GitHub, not CRAN or Bioconductor. cyCombine imports sva (Bioconductor) and kohonen (CRAN); CytoNorm imports flowCore and FlowSOM (Bioconductor). A conda environment file alone does not pin a GitHub-sourced R package reproducibly.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• config/upstream_lock.yaml pins a full 40-character commit for every resource, plus its licence, its adapter strategy, and the exact list of functions our adapters call.
  • scripts/fetch_upstream.sh materialises those commits.
  • Reproducible execution of the R backends requires the container definition in containers/, because the transitive CRAN and Bioconductor dependencies cannot be pinned by commit from R alone.
  • Runner dependencies (Python, Snakemake) are separate from task dependencies (R and its packages).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Without the container, cycombine reports not_available with the reason, and the Stage 6 gate for it is recorded as blocked rather than passed.
  • The audit scripts run in two modes: against an installed library when one is present, and against the pinned source otherwise. Both read a signature; neither infers one.

docs.title: 0005 — Evaluation partitions are frozen once, before any candidate runs
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: If a correction is allowed to re-derive the labels it is scored against, it is scored against a partition it created. cyCombine's own benchmarking vignette describes exactly this: correction-specific clustering changes the uncorrected EMD baseline.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Two namespaces, kept apart:

  • native — upstream-compatible mode. Upstream's own partitioning behaviour is preserved, including the moving uncorrected baseline. Results carry the native namespace and are never mixed with common numbers.
  • common — one frozen partition shared by every candidate: the same evaluation cells, the same labels, the same marker subset, the same comparison pairs.

Evaluation labels come from one of three tiers, and the tier and its confidence are carried on every metric record: user annotation (high), threshold gating in the declared coordinate system (medium, the default when no annotation exists), or clustering of the uncorrected baseline (low, flagged as potentially batch-driven and never sufficient on its own to support a recommendation).

Quantitative neighbourhood metrics are pinned to four settings recorded on every record: marker space, the evaluation marker mask, the declared per-marker scaling, Euclidean distance, and a declared k. UMAP is visualisation and is never the scoring coordinate system.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Candidate order cannot change labels or comparisons (tested).
  • A metric computed in native mode is not comparable with the same-named common metric, and the namespaces make that visible rather than implicit.

docs.title: 0006 — Success, ineligible and failed are three different things
docs.text: Status: accepted (Stage 0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The cheapest way to make a pipeline look complete is to let a missing dependency, an invalid comparison or a crashed method fall through as "no result", which a reader then interprets as "no problem".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• CorrectionStatus distinguishes success, ineligible, failed and not_available; MetricStatus distinguishes ok, ineligible, insufficient_data, undefined, failed and not_implemented; DecisionState is separate again from both.
  • A failed backend never returns the unchanged input. The identity candidate is the only thing allowed to return the baseline, and it is a genuine candidate that goes through the same validation, export and scoring path as any other.
  • Missing values are never zero. A near-zero denominator produces undefined, not a score stabilised with an epsilon.
  • Downstream components read status from records, never from the existence of a directory. stage_status builds the roster from the validated configuration and reports one entry per planned unit.
  • Relative reductions use the same eligible comparisons in numerator and denominator, so dropping an unavailable comparison cannot improve a candidate's standing.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The report has a "failures and limitations" section that is populated from records, and failed candidates stay visible in the comparison table.
  • A partial run is reportable as a partial run.
  • R exit zero requires a valid result envelope. Missing/malformed results and timeouts raise the checked boundary's existing failure type with logs; callers report the actual reason. Timeouts have no reported exit code. R execution uses a four-hour default and version probes a 30-second limit. Declared string arrays retain their list shape across the R/JSON/Python boundary.
  • Expected candidate execution/output errors (including invalid values, missing files, malformed JSON, timeouts and export I/O failures) produce a failure record and a traceback in logs/correct_<candidate>.log. A failed software-version probe cannot replace the original error. Invalid shared inputs, cancellation, unexpected programming defects and inability to persist the failure remain whole-run errors.
  • Before a correction retry, its old result, corrected H5AD and metric result are invalidated. Failed/partial exports are removed; only a successful correction exports a matrix. The old file cannot supply scores after a new attempt fails.
  • Backend names are checked during configuration validation. Candidate IDs must be non-empty directory names without path separators, so retry invalidation cannot traverse into another candidate's directory.

docs.title: When the honest answer is "don't correct"
docs.text:
Most batch-correction tools answer one question: how do I remove the batch effect? This vignette runs the case where the correct answer is you cannot, and here is why — and shows what a tool that refuses to say so would have done to your study.

Every state and reason below is from a real executed run (version 0.1.0, seed 473). The scenario is the shipped confounded example: two batches, no measured reference, and — the fatal property — the biological group of interest is perfectly confounded with the batch. Every case sample was measured in batch A; every control in batch B.

docs.title: 1. Run it
docs.text:
batchdx-cyto init my-project --example confounded
batchdx-cyto benchmark --config my-project/config/config.yaml \
    --outdir my-project/results/run1 --cores 4

docs.title: 2. What the decision said
docs.text:
recommended_candidate_id is null:

candidate state reason uncorrected below_design_floor 2 batch(es) present; the declared minimum is 3; no measured reference sample is shared across any pair of the batches under comparison cycombine_default insufficient_evidence at least one protected factor is perfectly confounded with the batch factor

docs.title: 3. Why this is the correct answer
docs.text:
With group and batch perfectly confounded, the group term and the batch term span the same subspace. Any "batch effect" the diagnostics find is also the biological effect of interest, and no algorithm — however clever — can tell them apart, because the data contains no information that distinguishes them. A correction that "succeeds" here has removed the biology, or kept it and called it batch; there is no third option.

Three design properties work together to make the refusal automatic and legible:

  1. The design audit classifies the contrast before any correction runs. The contingency of batch × group is computed from the sample manifest, the comparison is marked non_identifiable, and the cyCombine backend is marked ineligible with reason_code: batch_not_identifiable. This entry is non-overridable: the exploratory override (design.allow_exploratory_override) exists for eligibility failures that are a matter of judgement, and arithmetic unavailability is not one.
  2. The design floor stops the run from pretending. Two batches is below the declared design.minimum_batches (default 3), so every candidate is below_design_floor and the system produces descriptive output only. The floor is a configuration value with a declared origin, echoed into design_audit.json — not a hidden constant.
  3. Adding the factor as a covariate does not help, and the report says so. A common folk remedy for confounding is to throw the confounded factor into the model as a covariate. With perfect confounding there is nothing to estimate: the design matrix is rank-deficient. The audit states this explicitly instead of letting the user discover it in a reviewer comment.

docs.title: 4. What a leaderboard would have done
docs.text:
A tool that scores corrections and picks the best number would have "corrected" this data — the batch effect and the biology are the same signal, so removing one is trivially easy and looks spectacular on every alignment metric. The published study would then report that the group effect vanished after batch correction, which is exactly backwards: the group effect was the batch effect, and no one can say which.

The package's answer is the least dramatic possible output — a null recommendation, two named states, two reasons — and it is the only output that is scientifically honest. Abstention is a first-class outcome, not a failure path.

docs.title: 5. What you should do with such a design
docs.text: The package will not tell you how to fix your study, but the audit's structure points at what is missing: batches that contain both biological groups (so group and batch are estimable separately), and a measured technical reference shared across batches (so the technical component has ground truth). The paired-reference example is the minimal design that has both.

docs.text:
